items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Tropical Oceanography, Laboratory of Tropical Marine Bio-resources and Ecology, South China Sea Institute of Oceanology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Guangzhou 510301, China.; National Field Observation and Research Station (Hainan Sanya) for Marine Ecosystem, Tropical Marine Biological Research Station in Hainan, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Sanya 572000, China.; Key Laboratory of Tropical Marine Biotechnology of Hainan Province, Sanya Institute of Ocean Eco-Environmental Engineering, Sanya 572000, China.
items.abstract: Climate change threatens coral reefs globally, highlighting the need to understand mechanisms underlying coral holobiont resilience. Intertidal corals exhibit superior heat tolerance, yet the role of associated microbiomes remains unclear. By integrating field surveys, heat-stress experiments, and metagenomics, we compared intertidal and subtidal Porites lutea microbiomes. Our results show that intertidal P. lutea host bacterial communities are enriched in generalists with broad niche breadths and exhibit high functional redundancy in stress-response pathways. Under acute thermal stress, intertidal corals showed greater thermotolerance than subtidal corals. Concurrently, intertidal coral-associated bacterial communities maintained relatively stable taxonomic composition and functional integrity. Across habitats, preservation of photosynthetic efficiency ( F v / F m ) in the coral holobiont under heat stress was associated with higher bacterial generalist richness and functional redundancy. Together, these results suggest that long-term environmental variability may be associated with microbiome features consistent with functional buffering and holobiont stability. These findings may inform the design of synthetic microbial consortia to improve coral resilience under warming oceans.

items.title: Drug candidate CT7-1 promotes antitumor immunity by targeting SETMAR to activate cGAS-STING-IFN signaling in breast cancer
items.last_author_affiliation: Shengli Clinical Medical College of Fujian Medical University, Fujian Provincial Hospital, Fuzhou University Affiliated Provincial Hospital, Fuzhou 350001, China.
items.abstract: The discovery of previously unidentified anti–breast cancer agents with both high efficacy and favorable safety profiles remains an urgent and critical challenge. Recently, repurposing and modifying the anti-Alzheimer drug memantine have drawn growing interest to enhance its pharmacological properties. Here, we synthesized several memantine analogs, among which a honokiol-memantine hybrid named CT7-1 exhibited broad-spectrum and potent antitumor activity, particularly against breast cancer. Notably, CT7-1 suppressed breast cancer patient-derived organoid proliferation across diverse molecular subtypes while showing a superior toxicity profile in normal breast organoids relative to paclitaxel. In vivo, CT7-1 effectively suppressed tumor growth in immunocompromised and immunocompetent mouse models, with enhanced efficacy observed in the presence of an intact immune system. Integrated multiomics analyses revealed that CT7-1 reshaped the tumor microenvironment by increasing CD8 + T cell infiltration and activation, in addition to promoting major histocompatibility complex class I (MHC-I)–mediated antigen presentation. Mechanistically, CT7-1 directly bound to and inhibited SETMAR, leading to DNA damage and subsequent cGAS-STING pathway activation. This cascade resulted in the production of pro-inflammatory interferons and chemokines, ultimately up-regulating MHC-I expression. Clinically, high SETMAR expression correlated with poor prognosis, diminished immune cell infiltration, and inferior response to immunotherapy in patients with triple-negative breast cancer. In conclusion, we identify CT7-1 as a first-in-class honokiol-memantine hybrid that exerts potent antitumor effects by targeting SETMAR to activate the DNA damage-cGAS-STING-MHC-I axis, thereby enhancing T cell–mediated tumor immunity. This study provides convincing grounds for developing CT7-1 as a promising immunotherapeutic drug for breast cancer.

items.title: Immunotherapy response in TLS-positive solid tumors treated with regorafenib plus avelumab: the prospective, multicenter, open-label, phase 2 REGOMUNE trial
First-in-human results of NKT2152 monotherapy, an oral HIF-2α inhibitor, in advanced clear cell renal cell carcinoma: an open-label, multicenter, phase 1/2 study
Hippocampal reactivation of aversive experience promotes a slow-breathing recovery state
Maternal smoking in early pregnancy disrupts placental function through syncytiotrophoblast and macrophage dysregulation
Tuning curves as random projections
PFPTok enables efficient long-context genomic sequence modeling
A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families.
items.last_author_affiliation: Cambridge Institute for Medical Research, University of Cambridge, Cambridge, UK. jcr1003@cam.ac.uk.
items.abstract: To maintain infection in the human bloodstream, Plasmodium falciparum parasites undergo repeated cycles of invasion of and multiplication inside red blood cells (RBCs). Two protein families, the Erythrocyte binding-like (EBA) and Reticulocyte binding-like (Rh) proteins, are known to play a key role in invasion, mediating early stages of attachment of the P. falciparum merozoite to the host RBC. There is a degree of redundancy within these families, such that disrupting the function of individual EBA/Rh proteins in vitro is not sufficient to prevent invasion. By employing a novel approach to disrupt multiple EBA and Rh genes in combination, we systematically assess functional interdependency across these families for the first time. This analysis, and further characterisation of mutant parasites, reveals that disruption of some pairs of EBA/Rh ligands significantly impacts P. falciparum invasion, whereas others do not. Disruption of PfEBA175 in combination with either PfRh2b or PfRh4 significantly reduces parasite multiplication in vitro, indicating that the remaining EBA/Rh proteins cannot fully compensate for the absence of these three key invasion ligands. PfEBA175, PfRh2b and PfRh4 may therefore represent a critical nexus of the parasite invasion machinery, and combinatorial approaches that target these specific ligands could be a beneficial therapeutic approach.

items.title: Proximity labeling of the Listeria monocytogenes surface reveals pathogen control of a host deubiquitinase.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Biology, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Cambridge, MA, USA. rlamason@mit.edu.
items.abstract: Listeria monocytogenes navigates a crowded intracellular environment by recruiting host factors to its surface in order to hijack the host actin cytoskeleton for motility and cell-to-cell spread. Although these types of Listeria-host interactions are critical for infection, systematic characterization of this interface has been limited. Here, we implement the biotin ligase split-TurboID to profile host proteins recruited to the surface of L. monocytogenes during intracellular infection. We show that the host deubiquitinase CYLD is enriched at the pathogen surface. While CYLD promotes infection by suppressing innate immunity in macrophages, how L. monocytogenes recruits and appropriates CYLD function in other cell types has remained unclear. We demonstrate that L. monocytogenes uses the secreted effector Internalin C (InlC) to redirect CYLD to M1-linked linear ubiquitin at the bacterial poles. Despite its localization, CYLD does not deubiquitinate bacteria or regulate autophagic clearance in epithelial cells. Instead, CYLD and InlC protect L. monocytogenes from IFN-γ- and RNF213-dependent restriction of cell-to-cell spread. Overall, our work profiling the bacterial surface-host interactome has identified a mechanism by which InlC spatially reprograms CYLD activity to promote cell-to-cell spread in epithelial cells. These findings highlight how L. monocytogenes exploits a host deubiquitinase to perform cell-type-specific functions during infection.

items.title: CryoET imaging reveals that mitotic spindles are locally organized by microtubule density and Eg5 activity.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular Physiology and Biological Physics, University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA, USA. sz5j@virginia.edu.; Center for Membrane and Cell Physiology, University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA, USA. sz5j@virginia.edu.; Department of Cell Biology, University of Virginia School of Medicine, Charlottesville, VA, USA. sz5j@virginia.edu.
items.abstract: When eukaryotic cells divide, a mitotic spindle, composed of microtubule filaments interacting with molecular motors, self-assembles and is responsible for aligning and segregating chromosomes to the opposite daughter cells. Recent structural studies revealed that spindles are composed of short microtubules that do not span the full pole-to-chromosome distance. It remains unclear how these short, disconnected microtubules collectively assemble a bipolar spindle. Using cryo-electron tomography to map microtubule polarity in human spindles, we find that microtubules organize with consistent 8 nm wall-to-wall spacing. Spacing scales inversely with local microtubule density, consistent with organization by density-driven steric interactions, analogous to liquid crystal ordering. We find that the Eg5 motor establishes local antiparallel overlap independently of spindle bipolarity, while a balance of Eg5 and dynein regulates microtubule density to maintain spindle architecture. Together, these findings reveal the mesoscale principles by which cells build complex, self-healing cellular architectures from nanoscale building blocks.

items.title: Probing spin order via magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Physics, Harvard University, Cambridge, MA, USA. yacoby@g.harvard.edu.
items.abstract: Two-dimensional material platforms host a remarkable array of exotic correlated phases. Probing magnetic order in these systems is essential for understanding their underlying physics, yet dilute spin densities render conventional magnetic probes ineffective. Spin waves, or magnons, in quantum Hall ferromagnets (QHFM) have proven effective for probing the magnetic order in various symmetry-broken quantum Hall (QH) phases in graphene systems, but previous works have been limited to homojunction configurations within a single material. Here, we demonstrate magnon transmission across a monolayer-bilayer graphene quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunction-the first magnon transmission across quantum Hall ferromagnet heterojunctions, using one material as a magnon source to probe magnetic order in a distinct material. Generating magnons in monolayer graphene (MLG) at νMLG = 1, we detect their transmission through bilayer graphene (BLG) via nonlocal voltage measurements, revealing spin order in BLG symmetry-broken quantum Hall states. The transmission exhibits hallmark magnon signatures: a sharp onset at the Zeeman energy and systematic variation with Landau level filling, including suppression at νBLG = 4 and 8 where spin polarization vanishes. Our findings establish heterojunction magnon transmission as a powerful, modular probe of magnetic order, opening new avenues for investigating exotic quantum states across the rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional materials.

items.title: Framework desymmetrization enables partial pore space partition in metal-organic frameworks.
items.last_author_affiliation: The Institute for Advanced Studies (IAS), Wuhan University, Wuhan, PR China. zhao.xiang@whu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The pore-space-partition (PSP) has been recognized as a powerful strategy for boosting the uptake capacity of small gas molecules and has seen wide application in reticular chemistry. However, the most successful PSP platform-the partitioned-acs (pacs) net-has followed only one pattern since its inception over a decade ago: one partition agent per partition site, with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2). This fully partitioned architecture occupies all metal sites, eliminating open metal sites (OMSs) and compromising selectivity. Herein, we introduce a partial PSP concept accessed through a framework desymmetrization strategy. By replacing traditional high-symmetry D2h ligands with lower-symmetry C2h ligands (e.g., fumaric acid), we introduce structural distortions into the acs network, breaking the uniformity of partition sites and allowing partition agents to occupy only a fraction of available positions. This provides access to a PSP mechanism, namely part-pacs (partially partitioned-acs), with a general formula of [M3O(L1)3](L2)1/3. The part-pacs structures retain high acetylene capacity while exhibiting significantly enhanced selectivity compared to their fully partitioned analogues. Specifically, part-pacs-fum-tpa achieves C2H2/CO2 separation productivity nearly twice that of its full-pacs counterpart (1.92 mol kg-1 vs 0.98 mol kg-1).

items.title: Exaiptasia diaphana core microbiome members are lost under climate change conditions despite host thermal tolerance.
items.last_author_affiliation: University of California, Merced, Department of Cellular and Molecular Biology, Merced, CA, USA. esogin@gmail.com.; Botany and Plant Sciences, University of California, Riverside, Riverside, California, USA. esogin@gmail.com.
items.abstract: Acute and chronic exposure to elevated temperatures associated with Global Climate Change (GCC) threatens the structure and function of host-associated microbiomes, yet predicting microbial responses to heat stress remains challenging. We exposed two lines of the sea anemone, Exaiptasia diaphana, to acute and chronic thermal stress to quantify the impacts on cnidarian physiology and microbiome composition. Acute exposure caused rapid algal bleaching that was paired with pronounced shifts in bacteriome structure in both lines within 14 days of thermal exposure. Chronic exposure significantly affected the population structure, photo-physiology and bacteriome composition in only one host line, suggesting acclimation capacity depends on host-algal genetic backgrounds. Using 16S rRNA amplicon sequencing of 493 individuals sampled across 180 days, we found that sampling date explained nine-fold more variation in the microbiome composition than temperature exposure. Despite this temporal variation, we identified 16 indicator taxa that consistently changed in relative abundance under thermal stress. These taxa became central hubs in microbial association networks with increasing levels of thermal stress, suggesting they played key roles in bacteriome reorganization. As many of these taxa were present in other cnidarians, including reef-building corals, they may represent targets for conservation strategies that aim to enhance resilience on reefs.

items.title: Global arable land redistribution toward the tropics and drylands under human settlement expansion.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute on the Environment, University of Minnesota, St. Paul, MN, USA.
items.abstract: Arable land extent has undergone widespread changes across many regions worldwide through processes such as urban encroachment, forest conversion to agriculture, and dryland farming expansion. Yet an integrated understanding of global arable land dynamics remains limited. Using our self-developed arable land product integrated with global human settlement layers, Köppen-Geiger climate classifications, and historical land-use reconstructions, we show that the disproportionate climatic co-location of arable land and human settlements fundamentally structures global arable land dynamics. Across much of the climatically favorable Northern Hemisphere, earlier co-development of settlements and agriculture has increasingly shifted toward competition, with settlement expansion displacing cultivation from temperate regions and contributing to its expansion into adjacent arid zones. In contrast, low-latitude tropical regions continue to expand both systems at the expense of natural landscapes, partly driven by agricultural investment from Northern Hemisphere. Globally, these contrasting trajectories reveal a broader redistribution of agricultural pressure from climatically favorable regions toward less-exploited tropical and arid environments, linking settlement expansion and agricultural displacement to diverse environmental consequences including deforestation, biodiversity loss, groundwater depletion, and vegetation greening. These findings highlight the need to consider both local settlement-agriculture competition and broader agricultural redistribution when planning future food production and settlement growth.

items.title: Impression-R1 for radiological impression generation with multicenter benchmarking and prospective evaluations.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Radiology, The Second Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, Changsha, China. junliu123@csu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Radiological impressions are critical for clinical decision-making, yet expertise is unevenly distributed, and current large language models lack domain-specific reliability. We develop and evaluate Impression-R1, a domain-specialized large reasoning model for radiological impression generation, trained through an Imitation-Reasoning-Reinforcement pipeline integrating large-scale supervised learning, clinically conditioned reasoning, and radiology-aware reward optimization. Across 11,884 cases from six institutions and three public datasets spanning imaging modalities, anatomical regions, and diseases, including cross-lingual testing on English-language benchmarks, Impression-R1 outperforms or matches state-of-the-art general-purpose models. In a 200-case head-to-head evaluation, Impression-R1 shows stronger objective agreement with institution-derived reference impressions than all participating radiologists and subjective performance within the range of less-experienced radiologists under the study evaluation framework. Prospectively, radiologists rate its reasoning and clinical relevance highly. In a randomized within-reader study of 360 interpretations, AI assistance improves report quality (adjusted difference 0.28, 95% CI, 0.10-0.46) and reduces completion time by 27% (95% CI, 19.0%-33.9%); harmlessness scores are not significantly different (adjusted difference 0.08, 95% CI, -0.11-0.28). Here we show that Impression-R1 exemplifies a clinically informed framework for developing and evaluating domain-specialized reasoning models and can improve radiological reporting quality and efficiency, while requiring continued validation before broader clinical deployment.

items.title: Increasing prevalence and expanding diversity of tet(X4)-carrying Salmonella in China.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Veterinary Public Health and Safety, College of Veterinary Medicine, China Agricultural University, Beijing, China. szq@cau.edu.cn.; Key Laboratory of Animal Epidemiology of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, College of Veterinary Medicine, China Agricultural University, Beijing, China. szq@cau.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The plasmid-mediated tigecycline resistance gene tet(X4) threatens the efficacy of tigecycline. While prevalent in Escherichia coli across diverse ecological niches, its evolutionary trajectory in Salmonella remains underappreciated. Here, we conducted nationwide genomic surveillance of 42403 clinical nontyphoidal Salmonella isolates collected from diarrheal patients in China between 2014 and 2025, of which 102 were tet(X4)-positive. Although the overall prevalence remained low, detection showed a statistically significant upward trend over 2019-2025. Importantly, the newly accrued 2025 data were broadly consistent with short-term forecasts generated by the beta regression model, providing partial support for short-term trend consistency. Genomic analyses showed that tet(X4) remained concentrated in ST34 but was also detected in additional sequence types, including ST469, ST8971, ST11 and one isolate with an unassigned ST, across multiple provinces, indicating broader geographic representation and genetic diversification. Plasmid analyses likewise revealed broader replicon diversity, with the dominant IncHI1A/IncHI1B/IncFIA background accompanied by less frequent IncHI2/IncHI2A, IncI1(Alpha) and IncFIA/IncFIB/IncFIC. Phylogenetic analyses further revealed shared clustering of the dominant plasmid background across host species and bacterial genera, consistent with cross-host and cross-genus circulation.

items.title: Deuteration of arenes in D2O exclusively driven by single-atom Pt sites under visible light.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Bioinspired Interfacial Materials Science, School of Nano Science and Technology, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China. yitaodai@ustc.edu.cn.; School of Chemistry and Materials Science, University of Science and Technology of China, Hefei, China. yitaodai@ustc.edu.cn.; Suzhou Key Laboratory of Water Environment Science and Technology, Suzhou Institute for Advanced Research, University of Science and Technology of China, Suzhou, China. yitaodai@ustc.edu.cn.; Jiangxi Fangzhu Pharmaceutical Co. Ltd., Xinyu, China. yitaodai@ustc.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Deuterated arenes play crucial roles in medicinal chemistry and materials science (e.g., psychotropic drugs and deuterated OLEDs). However, the desired late-stage deuteration via conventional hydrogen isotope exchange methods always demands expensive isotopic reagents (e.g., D2, C6D6, or C2H5OD), metal complex catalysts, or harsh conditions ( ≥ 120 oC, 20 bar H2). Here, we report a single-atom photocatalytic strategy for efficient deuteration of electron-rich arenes using D2O as the deuterium source. Under visible light irradiation at ambient temperature in an inert atmosphere, a single-atom photocatalyst (Pt1/TiO2) affords high deuterium incorporation across 54 electron-rich arene substrates. The protocol is mild, sustainable, and scalable: gram-scale synthesis of deuterated arenes (11.98 g, 100 mmol) was successfully realized. Mechanistic studies indicate that the catalytically active sites are primarily Pt-O coordinate bonds, whose light-modulated charge distribution facilitates a possible electrophilic platinization pathway for C-H activation before H/D exchange.

items.title: Cryo-EM reveals major proteolysis independent substrate rearrangements in a complement C5 convertase surrogate complex(es).
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Molecular Biology and Genetics, Aarhus University, Aarhus C, Denmark. gra@mbg.au.dk.
items.abstract: Despite extensive structural analysis of the complement cascade, a detailed understanding of complement C5 activation is lacking. Here we show using cryo-EM that C5 in complex with the CVFBb surrogate convertase undergoes a proteolysis independent two-step rearrangement to a C5* conformation that enables the C5 scissile bond to reach the catalytic site of the Bb protease. C5* can form a complex with C6 and initiate membrane attack complex formation without C5 cleavage. Moreover, we observe an unusual convertase conformation where Bb rotates 155° relative to CVFBb in the putative Michaelis complex. This work demonstrates that the C5* conformation is functionally relevant and can help rationalize the mode of action for known C5 inhibitors, and we propose that large Bb rotations may allow the endogenous surface bound C5 convertases to cleave in trans C5 bound to a neighboring C3b molecule, presenting a refined model of C5 cleavage in vivo.

items.title: Serine supplementation reinvigorates anti-tumor immunity by counteracting tumor cell SLC1A4-induced T cell starvation.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Urology, The Affiliated Hospital of Xuzhou Medical University, Jiangsu Key Laboratory of Immunity and Metabolism, Jiangsu International Laboratory of Immunity and Metabolism, Department of Pathogenic Biology and Immunology, School of Basic Medicine and Life Sciences, Xuzhou Medical University, Xuzhou, Jiangsu, China. jumingyan@xzhmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: While serine restriction is known to suppress tumor cell proliferation, its therapeutic application remains challenging. Unexpectedly, we show that serine supplementation therapeutically suppressed tumor growth and metastasis in multiple preclinical models while simultaneously boosting CD8⁺ T-cell proliferation and effector functions. Mechanistically, IFNγ released by activated T cells triggers STAT1-dependent induction of the serine transporter SLC1A4 in tumor cells, enabling them to deplete extracellular serine and thereby starve infiltrating CD8⁺ T cells. Genetic deletion of SLC1A4 reverses this metabolic hijack, restores serine availability within the tumor microenvironment, and markedly enhances anti-tumor immunity. Dietary serine supplementation not only replicates the immune-activating effects of SLC1A4 loss but also overcomes resistance to PD-1 blockade, producing durable control in checkpoint-refractory tumors. Collectively, these data position serine supplementation rather than restriction as a readily translatable strategy to reinvigorate exhausted T cells and improve immunotherapy outcomes.

items.title: Wavelength selective fragmentation of metastable photoresponsive platelets via light irradiation.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Bio-based Fiber Materials, Zhejiang Sci-Tech University, Hangzhou, China. tongzz@zstu.edu.cn.; Zhejiang Sci-Tech University Shengzhou Innovation Research Institute, Shengzhou, China. tongzz@zstu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Polymer lamellar crystals commonly consisting of folded chains are frequently formed since they are kinetically favorable. Hence, the metastability of polymer crystals can be regulated by crystallization pathways, and the thinner lamellar crystals display a tendency to transform into thicker crystals via lamellar thickening process. Herein, we report that photoresponsive two-dimensional (2D) platelets with low metastability undergo controllable fragmentation upon light irradiation. Mechanistic studies indicate that the metastability within a single platelet particle is heterogeneous across different domains. Light irradiation triggers lamellar thickening preferentially within less stable domains decorated with photoresponsive molecules, leading to site-specific fragmentation. To illustrate the utility of light-stimulated fragmentation, wavelength selective fragmentation of 2D segmented platelets with spatially defined photoresponsive molecules is achieved upon light irradiation, yielding 2D hollow platelet structure. This important feature holds significant promise for advanced applications such as spatially resolved therapeutic delivery systems, thereby broadening the functional scope of 2D nanomaterials.

items.title: Glacial CO2 drawdown by plankton metabolic balance.
items.last_author_affiliation: University of Liverpool, Liverpool, UK.
items.abstract: Which mechanisms caused the Holocene-versus-Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) atmospheric carbon dioxide (CO2) difference? This longstanding question is crucial for characterizing glacial-interglacial cycles and using LGM climate information in climate predictions. We argue that the metabolic temperature dependence of epipelagic plankton is an important mechanism. Autotrophic plankton metabolisms are less sensitive to temperature than heterotrophic ones. Colder waters can thereby export and thus sequester more carbon in the deep ocean. We develop a theoretical model from Metabolic Theory of Ecology principles, then validate its predictions with empirical data compilations. We then use temperature reconstructions to estimate the plankton metabolism-driven LGM CO2 anomaly. Holding all other conditions at their pre-industrial state, such as net primary production and buffering capacity, we find that this mechanism represents a 6.2 ± 0.9ppm per degree global mean sea surface temperature change feedback, and can potentially explain 20 ± 5ppm, or  ~ 1/4 of the total  ~ 90ppm LGM CO2 anomaly. We diagnose a similar 18ppm using model data from an intermediate complexity Earth System Model that considers glacial-interglacial differences in nutrient limitation and primary production. Our findings are consistent with several temperature-driven mechanisms acting concertedly to modulate glacial-interglacial CO2 variations.

items.title: Tree shrew more closely recapitulates primate spermatogenesis than the mouse in cross-species single-cell transcriptomic analyses.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Genetic Evolution & Animal Models, Yunnan Key Laboratory of Animal Models and Human Disease Mechanisms, and KIZ-CUHK Joint Laboratory of Bioresources and Molecular Research in Common Diseases, Kunming Institute of Zoology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Kunming, Yunnan, China. zhengp@mail.kiz.ac.cn.; Kunming College of Life Science, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, Kunming, Yunnan, China. zhengp@mail.kiz.ac.cn.; National Research Facility for Phenotypic & Genetic Analysis of Model Animals (Primate Facility), National Resource Center for Non-Human Primates, Yunnan Engineering Center on Brain Disease Models, Kunming Institute of Zoology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, Kunming, Yunnan, China. zhengp@mail.kiz.ac.cn.
items.abstract: The rapid evolution of spermatogenesis limits the utility of mouse models for studying human spermatogenesis because some genes are absent or divergent in mice. Primate models face practical and ethical constraints, whereas tree shrews are closely related to primates and suitable for laboratory research. Here we integrate histology and single-nucleus RNA sequencing data from human, rhesus macaque, mouse and tree shrew testes to assess the tree shrew as a model of human spermatogenesis. We show that transcriptional landscapes in tree shrew spermatogenic cells, particularly late-stage spermatids, more closely resemble those of primates than mice. Conservation and enrichment analyses identify two core gene modules shared among humans, macaques and tree shrews but distinct in mice. Gene expression trajectories also align between tree shrews and primates, including for genes without murine orthologs. Immunostaining and RNA-FISH support representative expression patterns. These findings define contexts in which tree shrews can complement existing models of human spermatogenesis and male infertility.

items.title: Secondary organic aerosol formation from sequential oxidation of toluene and cresols.
items.last_author_affiliation: Aerosol Physics Laboratory, Tampere University, Tampere, Finland. siddharth.iyer@tuni.fi.
items.abstract: Cresols are important urban emissions that can form multiple oxygen containing condensable vapors when they react with OH radicals in the atmosphere. These molecules contribute to secondary organic aerosols that have strong implications on climate and human health. In this work, we present flow reactor oxidation experiments demonstrating the rapid (sub-second) formation of condensable vapors with up to 10 oxygen atoms from the three cresol isomers (ortho-, para- and meta-cresol) under atmospheric conditions. Our quantum chemical calculations reveal that initial OH additions to the hydroxyl containing carbon atom lead to geminal diol intermediates that are critical to the rapid formation of condensable vapors from cresols and their key oxidation product, 3-methylcatechol. Incorporating these autoxidation mechanisms into model simulations shows that they contribute significantly to secondary organic aerosol composition. These results could explain the strong multi-generational contributions to aerosol from toluene and cresol, enabling a more accurate assessment of their climate and health impacts.

items.title: Evolutionary oxidation of proteins in Earth's history.
items.last_author_affiliation: Roy M. Huffington Department of Earth Sciences, Southern Methodist University, Dallas, TX, USA.
items.abstract: Evidence for Earth's oxygenation during the Great Oxidation Event (GOE) and Neoproterozoic Oxidation Event (NOE) comes primarily from the geological record. We report rising oxidation state of carbon (Zc) in proteins over billion-year timescales, a consistent trend recovered from diverse genomic datasets. Combining statistical and thermodynamic modeling, we link this trend to environmental drivers including Earth's progressive oxygenation and secular cooling. The oxidation trend appears in the amino acid composition of modern genomes from methanogens and sulfur-cycling organisms, phylostratigraphic gene age groups in eukaryotes, and reconstructed ancestral sequences for Rubisco, nitrogenase, thioredoxin, and 3-isopropylmalate dehydrogenase (IPMDH). Major Zc steps broadly overlap the GOE but do not exactly coincide with it; uncertainties in phylogenetic age and limited spatial associations complicate direct comparison with geochemical proxies. Gene age groups in unicellular, but not multicellular, eukaryotes show a second rise of protein Zc around the NOE. These widespread genomic signatures of protein oxidation are consistent with a thermodynamic hypothesis in which energy minimization directs protein sequence evolution across metabolic functions.

items.title: A training-free, domain-extensible LLM-based approach for automated extraction of standardized preparation procedures.
items.last_author_affiliation: Chemical Engineering Department & Centro de Química Estrutural - Institute of Molecular Sciences, Instituto Superior Técnico, University of Lisbon, Lisbon, Portugal. pedro.f.mendes@tecnico.ulisboa.pt.
items.abstract: Millions of synthesis procedures have been published, but their meta-analysis, important for identifying successful synthesis patterns, is difficult due to varied reporting structures. Using this information requires converting unstructured text into a precise sequence of actions, which requires understanding domain jargon, a challenge usually addressed by fine-tuning models on labeled data. We present a simple, training-free workflow for laboratory action extraction that works across fields, encoding domain knowledge through explicit action sets and using powerful, readily available Large Language Models, or LLMs. Applied to zeolite synthesis, a widely used class of porous materials, our approach outperforms existing open-source tools and delivers context-aware results with open, locally runnable LLMs. It also matches state-of-the-art, field-specific models in their own domains, highlighting the generalization capabilities of current LLMs. The methodology showcased,  along with the open algorithms made available, allow chemists to evaluate action sets, screen LLMs, and digitize laboratory procedures accurately with minimal effort.

items.title: Viral tRNA-like structure hijacks host ribosomes for poly(A)-independent translation.
items.last_author_affiliation: State Key Laboratory of Genetics and Development of Complex Phenotypes, School of Life Sciences, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. linjinzhong@fudan.edu.cn.; Shanghai Institute of Infectious Disease and Biosecurity, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. linjinzhong@fudan.edu.cn.; Center for mRNA Translational Research, Fudan University, Shanghai, China. linjinzhong@fudan.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Positive-sense RNA viruses often use 3' tRNA-like structures (TLSs) instead of poly(A) tails to capture the host translation machinery. While TLSs resemble canonical tRNAs and engage host factors, their ability to directly recruit ribosomes has remained unresolved. Here, we present cryo-electron microscopy snapshots of the histidine-accepting TLS (TLSHis) from tobacco mosaic virus bound to the tobacco 60S subunit, the 80S ribosome, and the 80S-tRNAiMet initiation complex. Across these states, TLSHis is consistently anchored to the L1 stalk of 60S, even under cycloheximide treatment, yet remains dynamic on the 40S subunit. Structural analysis shows that TLSHis transitions from the E-site to an adjacent Z-site to accommodate initiator tRNA. Functional assays show that TLSHis preferentially associates with ribosomal subunits over polysomes and can substitute for a poly(A) tail to promote robust cap-dependent translation. These results provide structural and mechanistic evidence that the viral tRNA mimic exploits the tRNA-exit channel to stabilize initiation-competent ribosomes and drive poly(A)-independent translation.

items.title: KMT2B facilitates long-range gene regulation through LINE1 elements.
items.last_author_affiliation: Institute of Biomedicine and Biotechnology of Cantabria (IBBTEC), CSIC/Universidad de Cantabria, Santander, Spain. alvaro.rada@unican.es.
items.abstract: Transcriptional regulation is tightly linked to chromatin organization, with H3K4me3 marking active and bivalent promoters. In embryonic stem cells, KMT2B deposits H3K4me3 at bivalent promoters, yet loss of H3K4me3 at these sites leaves developmental gene transcription largely unaltered. Here, we show that, in both mouse embryonic stem cells and during differentiation, the primary role of KMT2B is not to counteract Polycomb-mediated repression at bivalent promoters. Instead, we uncover a distinct regulatory function for KMT2B at the CG-rich 5'UTR of young LINE-1 elements. KMT2B binds LINE-1 5'UTRs and maintains their active chromatin state (H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H4K16ac) while preventing repressive H3K9me3 accumulation. Using complementary genomic methods and targeted deletions, we show that KMT2B-bound LINE-1 elements act as enhancers modulating neighboring gene expression in embryonic stem cells and, particularly, during differentiation. Our findings define KMT2B regulatory functions at LINE-1 repeats and highlight transposable elements as key components of long-range gene expression control.

items.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing.
items.last_author_affiliation: LBEN, Bioengineering Institute, École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Lausanne, Switzerland. aleksandra.radenovic@epfl.ch.
items.abstract: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy (  V B -   ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of  V B -   by up to 45× at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A quasi type-I band alignment at the PbI2-defected hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives  V B -   excitation. This process is compatible with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

items.title: The accuracy-safety trade-off of large reasoning models in clinical diagnostics.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Biomedical Engineering, Tsinghua Medicine, Tsinghua University, Beijing, China. hyzhou@tsinghua.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) offer potential advantages for clinical diagnosis over standard large language models (LLMs), yet their utility and safety remain unclear. Here we show, on AIMS-LDR, a long-context diagnostic reasoning benchmark built upon real-world electronic health records, covering six matched model pairs and 12 specialties, that LRMs generate over 34% more false positive diagnoses and show approximately 40% lower reproducibility than their LLM counterparts, while making more accurate primary diagnoses and more clinically relevant differentials. Experiments confirm this trade-off across prompt designs, model hyperparameters, and evaluation paradigms. A structured collaboration model, in which the LRM broadens diagnostic coverage and the clinician verifies reliability, increases diagnostic accuracy by 20% and reduces false positives by 44% in a 15-physician validation study. These results, obtained under controlled retrospective conditions, suggest that pairing LRM reasoning with physician oversight may support safer and more accurate diagnostic decision-making, warranting prospective validation before clinical deployment.

items.title: Systematic comparison of affinity plasma proteomic technologies across multiple cohorts reveals generalizability of proteomic prediction.
items.last_author_affiliation: Informatics and Predictive Sciences, Research, Bristol Myers Squibb, Cambridge, MA, USA. bbsun92@outlook.com.
items.abstract: Emergence of biobank level proteomic datasets with extensive phenotype linkage has significantly improved our understanding of proteomic drivers in health and ushered in a flurry of disease risk prediction models. However, differences in cohorts and proteomic assays can significantly undermine transferability of proteomic models, severely limiting their general use. In this study, we generate and harmonize comparisons of two leading multiplex affinity-based proteomic platforms (Olink and SomaScan) across 11 independent cohorts. We find key factors contributing to platform disparities and establish a high-quality set of 757 protein probe-pairs consistently correlated across cohorts as a reference for new emerging studies. To investigate the impact on proteomic prediction, we train models to predict age, body mass index and 15 common diseases, evaluating performance across multiple independent cohorts and platforms. We find systematic deterioration in model performance across platforms, especially without filtering for probe correlations, and a U-shaped effect in model transferability reflecting a trade-off between cross-platform protein consistency and biological relevance. The optimal cross-platform correlation cut-off varied between traits, with 0.3-0.4 as most prevalent. Our study highlights practical considerations for assessing proteomic model performance across platforms and cohorts, offering guidance for robust protein biomarker development, disease prediction, and drug targeting.

items.title: Ki-67, the chromosome periphery and de-compartmentalisation each contribute to nucleophosmin mislocalisation in acute myeloid leukaemia.
items.last_author_affiliation: Translational Medical Sciences, Biodiscovery Institute, University of Nottingham, Nottingham, United Kingdom. Daniel.Booth@nottingham.ac.uk.
items.abstract: The mitotic chromosome periphery (MCP) is an important chromosome compartment but links to disease remains elusive. Here we define the mitosis-specific, Ki-67 interactome, identifying additional MCP components and revealing that MCP genes are commonly mutated in cancer, including nucleophosmin (NPM1). Acute myeloid leukaemia (AML)-specific NPM1 mutations (NPM1c+), result in protein mislocalisation (nucleolus to cytoplasm). We demonstrate that NPM1c+ fails to adequately bind to the MCP, instead forming aggregates during mitosis. We also report that, de-compartmentalisation at mitotic onset allows formation of NPM1wt/c+ multimers. These mislocalisation mechanisms contribute to a significant hinderance of NPM1 re-entry into daughter cell nucleoli. Enhancing MCP loading capacity via Ki-67 overexpression resulted in increased MCP-bound NPM1c+ during mitosis and greater yield of nucleolar NPM1c+. Ki-67 expression demonstrated a significant interaction with NPM1 mutation status on AML patient overall survival, whereby higher Ki-67 was associated with increased hazard in NPM1wt but reduced hazard in NPM1c+ patients. This work reveals mechanistic insight into AML and evidence that the MCP has untapped therapeutic potential.

items.title: Stabilization of insulin receptor mRNA by Star-PAP in metabolic homeostasis.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Endocrine and Metabolic Diseases, Shanghai Institute of Endocrine and Metabolic Diseases, Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine, Shanghai, China. wangjq@shsmu.edu.cn.; Shanghai National Clinical Research Center for Metabolic Diseases, Key Laboratory for Endocrine and Metabolic Diseases of the National Health Commission of the PR China, Shanghai National Center for Translational Medicine, Shanghai, China. wangjq@shsmu.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Conserved polyadenylation b3y poly(A) polymerases (PAPs) is essential for mRNA stability, yet its metabolic functions remain unclear. Here we identify a rare variant p.D469N (Asp469Asn) in Star-PAP present in lean individuals but absent in obese cases. Adipose-specific Star-PAP knockout mice develop progressive adipose tissue loss, hepatic steatosis, and severe insulin resistance, phenocopying human lipodystrophy. Mechanistically, Star-PAP directly binds the insulin receptor (InsR) mRNA 3'-UTR to stabilize its transcript. Both deletion of Star-PAP and p.D469N variant decrease InsR mRNA maturation. Star-PAP deficiency impairs insulin receptor signaling and adipocyte lipid storage, while restoring InsR in adipocytes partially ameliorates the lipodystrophic phenotypes. Notably, Star-PAP deficiency disrupts acetyl-CoA homeostasis secondary to insulin signaling defects, accompanied by reduced histone acetylation at fatty acid synthesis genes. Pyruvate supplementation effectively restores acetyl-CoA levels and histone acetylation, thereby rescuing the gene expression and lipogenesis. Together, our results identify Star-PAP-mediated RNA polyadenylation as a mechanism governing adipose mass, positioning Star-PAP as a key regulator of insulin receptor signaling and lipodystrophy.

items.title: Layer-wise Prediction for Interpretation of Hidden Representations in Deep Neural Networks through Evolving Probability Distributions.
items.last_author_affiliation: Chongqing Key Laboratory of Brain-Inspired Cognitive Computing and Educational Rehabilitation for Children with Special Needs, Chongqing Normal University, Chongqing, China.
items.abstract: The sequential architecture of DNNs enables accurate predictions by encoding input features, yet their limited interpretability and transparency during forward propagation undermine the credibility of predictions. Therefore, we propose layer-wise prediction for interpretation method (LPI), which involves mapping the representation from each layer to a probability distribution, explaining the hidden-layer prediction process. To ensure interpretation fidelity to DNN mechanisms, we employ a reconstruction strategy to map probability distributions back to hidden layer features while reducing their influence on model prediction. Meanwhile, we define a rank-index metric to quantify the consistency of probability distribution evolution. Furthermore, we show how each hidden layer probability distribution evolves consistently during DNN forward propagation. Experiments on various models show that LPI achieves superior performance in consistency, stability, fidelity and certainty, outperforming AdditionalLayer, SDN, MetaGF, and DFS. Notably, LPI not only enhances deep learning interpretability but also provides valuable insights into reliable and credible model security assessment.

items.title: Cascade electrosynthesis of glycolic acid from ethylene and oxygen with an energy efficiency of 62.9.
items.last_author_affiliation: School of Materials Science and Engineering, Peking University, Beijing, P. R. China. guosj@pku.edu.cn.; Liaoning Binhai Laboratory, Liaoning, China. guosj@pku.edu.cn.
items.abstract: The high pollution and low purity associated with the conventional formaldehyde carbonylation process for glycolic acid (GA) production have motivated the search for alternative green pathway. Herein, we report a cascade conversion strategy integrating oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), ethylene oxidation, and ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR) for GA electrosynthesis. This approach achieves high energy efficiency at industrial current density levering generated hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) as an oxidant. The Faraday efficiency (FE) of GA at whole scheme can reach 93.5% at 300 mA cm-2. By replacing EG with ethylene and O2 as raw materials, the ORR-ethylene oxidation-EGOR cascade conversion strategy shows improved energy conversation efficiency of 62.9% and significantly reduces its total outlay cost. Economic analysis reveals that the net profit of the cascade system reaches $26.8 million with a 30-year electrolyzer lifespan, which is 5.22 and 1.97 times higher than that of isolated ORR and EGOR systems.

items.title: LytU is a bridge-link isopeptidase that contributes to vancomycin resistance in Staphylococcus aureus.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Chemistry, Nanoscience Center, University of Jyvaskyla, P.O. Box 35, Jyvaskyla, Finland. Perttu.Permi@jyu.fi.; Department of Biological and Environmental Science, Nanoscience Center, University of Jyvaskyla, P.O. Box 35, Jyvaskyla, Finland. Perttu.Permi@jyu.fi.; Institute of Biotechnology, Helsinki Institute of Life Science, University of Helsinki, P.O. Box 65, Helsinki, Finland. Perttu.Permi@jyu.fi.
items.abstract: Emergence of antimicrobial resistance is a pressing global issue. Although myriads of mechanisms for survival against antimicrobial pressure have surfaced, one key strategy is the structural modification of peptidoglycan, the main defense line in Gram-positive bacteria e.g., notorious pathogen Staphylococcus aureus. Here we show that the recently identified peptidoglycan hydrolase (PGH) LytU is an unusual catalyst in the lysostaphin (M23B) family of zinc-endopeptidases that hydrolyze the glycyl-glycine peptide bond in S. aureus. Unlike any other PGH recognized thus far, LytU hydrolyzes the isopeptide bond between the lysine ε amino group and pentaglycine, thus functioning as a bridge-link hydrolase. We discovered that LytM and LytU are functionally non-redundant, and they contribute to the cell wall remodeling at different stages of PG maturation. Additionally, we demonstrate that LytU particularly targets the PG precursor, pGly-Lipid II, and its overexpression leads to growth inhibition and a less densely cross-linked cell wall, which increases susceptibility to lysostaphin. Interestingly, LytU expression enhances resistance to the glycopeptide vancomycin, the drug of last resort against S. aureus.

items.title: Aberrant thymic architecture and enhanced interferon signaling in Down syndrome.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Hematology, St Jude Children's Research Hospital, Memphis, TN, USA. john.crispino@stjude.org.
items.abstract: Individuals with Down syndrome (DS) have an elevated risk of autoimmune disease, particularly celiac disease, type 1 diabetes, and autoimmune hypothyroidism. In DS, thymi show characteristic structural and cellular changes, but the connection between these and the propensity to autoimmune disease is still unclear. Here we present a cell atlas from single cell RNA-sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics of age-matched thymi from infants with and without DS, which might contribute to filling this knowledge gap. DS does not significantly alter CD34+ diversity in the thymus; however, the gene expression changes we observe indicate altered differentiative potential in DS CD34+ cells. Although many genes involved in T-cell development and function (including USP16, RUNX1 and ETS2) are located on chromosome 21, several important T cell regulatory genes that are located on other chromosomes also change in DS. In contrast, CD34- DS thymocytes are characterised by maturation defects. CD34+ progenitors and proliferating DP thymocytes are in a functional state of chronic interferon activation. In summary, we identify several notable differences in key functional cellular subsets and pathways within the DS thymus, providing insights into the spatiotemporal dynamics of the thymic environment for this genetic condition.

items.title: Lesion penetration predicts tuberculosis treatment shortening through a validated translational tool to de-risk development.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Bioengineering and Therapeutic Sciences, University of California San Francisco, San Francisco, CA, USA. rada.savic@ucsf.edu.
items.abstract: Anti-tuberculosis (TB) drugs must reach the disease site to be effective, but complex TB pathology limits drug distribution and efficacy, as bacteria in the necrotic center of lung cavities are difficult to access and kill. Our study generates the most comprehensive database of site-of-disease distribution for 24 drugs and drug candidates in a rabbit model of cavitary TB. We validate a lung lesion penetration model with clinical data and develop an integrated approach that combines microenvironment-specific pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics. Next, we simulate site-of-disease coverage of shortened regimens tested in major Phase 3 trials over the past decade, allowing direct comparisons with trial outcomes. We propose that regimens including at least two drugs achieving bactericidal concentrations in pulmonary cavities are more likely to meet primary clinical endpoints in patients with cavitary disease. Our translational platform constitutes a validated tool to support drug evaluation, smart regimen design, and de-risking of late-stage trials.

items.title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction.
items.last_author_affiliation: Key Laboratory of Jiangsu Province for Chemical Pollution Control and Resources Reuse, School of Environmental and Biological Engineering, Nanjing University of Science and Technology, Nanjing, China. lijsh@njust.edu.cn.
items.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are ideal for precious metal recovery due to their high surface areas and tunable binding sites. However, the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer, resulting in poor site accessibility and limited extraction capacities. Herein, we report a quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery. By incorporating outward-pointing hydroxyl groups, the local conformation of the imine-linked skeleton is effectively locked via inter-chain hydrogen bonding (ICHB), which suppresses molecular torsion and promotes ordered assembly of the 1D chains into a quasi-2D crystalline architecture. This structural rigidification creates unobstructed ion-diffusion pathways and maximizes the exposure of active sites for rapid [AuCl4]- capture and reduction. Remarkably, under mild thermal and vibratory stimulation, gold nanoparticles form in situ and aggregate, yielding a high gold extraction capacity of 5082.32 mg g-1. Theoretical calculations demonstrate that ICHB-induced structural planarization creates a cooperative coordination environment and optimizes the energetic landscape for dechlorination, synergistically promoting guest enrichment and interfacial gold reduction. This work establishes a new blueprint for creating COFs with exposed active sites via inter-chain assembly, offering a scalable approach to maximize site accessibility and electron transfer for selective gold capture.

items.title: CADS: a comprehensive anatomical dataset and segmentation for whole-body anatomy in computed tomography.
items.last_author_affiliation: Department of Quantitative Biomedicine, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland.
items.abstract: Volumetric computed tomography (CT) segmentation supports quantitative image analysis, but most AI-based methods remain organ-specific, with fragmented models, inconsistent label definitions, and heterogeneous training and evaluation protocols. Here we present CADS, a unified data-model framework for scalable and generalizable whole-body CT segmentation. We construct a SNOMED-CT-referenced anatomical label space harmonizing heterogeneous cohorts from over 100 imaging centers, yielding complete annotations of 167 structures across 22,022 CT volumes and markedly expanding anatomical coverage and scale beyond existing resources. To complete labels on sparsely annotated CTs, we combine self-training with shape-informed quality control based on neural implicit functions, curating high-quality pseudo-labels. Trained on this resource, CADS shows robust whole-body segmentation across distribution shifts and improved performance relative to state-of-the-art approaches across 18 public datasets. We further validate it in an independent, expert-reviewed real-world oncology cohort of 2864 CTs. The curated dataset, pretrained models, and user-friendly software together provide an accessible, reproducible foundation for large-scale anatomical segmentation and computational anatomy research.

items.title: Efficient 3D Cell Tracking by Integer Programming Guided by Self-Supervised Division Scores
items.abstract: Recognizing divisions in cell tracking is difficult when cells are densely packed and divide frequently. A daughter can lie closer to a neighbor than to its mother, misleading distance-based linking. Visual cues can reduce such errors, but learning them often requires manual lineage annotations, which are particularly costly for 3D data. We propose an efficient self-supervised tracker trained without manual lineage annotations, using biological priors to extract reliable divisions from its distance-based tracks as labels. Networks trained on these labels predict division scores from mother-daughter images and the mother's temporal context to guide an integer linear program in resolving competing daughter assignments. Among the evaluated trackers, ours ranks first on one of three C. elegans datasets and second to a supervised tracker on the other two. It also needs less than half the training or tuning time of any compared method. Code is available at https://github.com/AnAncientMoon/Divtrack.

items.title: Baseline Predictors of Craving Reduction Following Non-Invasive Neuromodulation: A Computational Modeling Approach
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Psychology, Seoul National University, Seoul 08826, Republic of Korea; Department of Brain and Cognitive Sciences, Seoul National University, Seou
items.abstract: Background: Alcohol craving is a clinically relevant symptom with an established neurobiological basis and has emerged as a treatment target. Non-invasive neuromodulation has shown potential for reducing craving, but substantial inter-individual variability in response is a pervasive challenge. This study examined whether baseline computational parameters predicted treatment response following neuromodulation. Methods: This secondary analysis of an open-label, randomized trial included 58 individuals with subclinical alcohol use who received transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS), transcranial photobiomodulation (tPBM), or combined taVNS + tPBM for five weeks. Baseline computational measures from Delay Discounting, Choice under Risk and Ambiguity, and Loss Aversion Tasks were examined as predictors of treatment response. Elastic net regularization was used to identify markers associated with Reliable Change Index (RCI)-defined responder status, alongside demographic variables, intervention condition, and baseline craving. Results: Of the 58 participants, 24 were classified as treatment responders. The elastic net model showed a mean test AUC of 0.66 across 1,000 iterations, indicating modest predictive performance. Baseline craving, intervention condition, age, sex, and computational modeling parameters contributed to responder status: Higher loss aversion and lower risk sensitivity were associated with a greater likelihood of responder status. Conclusions: Baseline computational measures, particularly loss aversion and risk sensitivity, may serve as candidate behavioral markers associated with craving reduction following non-invasive neuromodulation. Given the open-label design, these findings represent an initial proof-of-concept. Future sham-controlled studies are needed to determine whether these parameters are associated with stimulation-specific responses or more general susceptibility to behavioral change.

items.title: Development and validation of LC-MS/MS bioanalytical methods to support the clinical pharmacology studies of COMP360, a form of synthetic psilocybin
items.abstract: COMP360, a form of synthetic psilocybin (PSY), is being developed for the treatment of treatment-resistant depression (TRD) and post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). Orally-administered PSY is rapidly cleaved to the active moiety, psilocin (PSI), which undergoes further metabolism to psilocin-O-glucuronide (PSIG) and 4-hydroxyindole-3-acetic acid (4-HIAA). Methods for the quantification of PSY and its metabolites in plasma (PSY - 0.5 to 500 ng/mL; PSI - 0.5 to 200 ng/mL; PSIG - 1.0 to 400 ng/mL; 4-HIAA - 5 to 2000 ng/mL), and PSI in human urine (0.5 to 200 ng/mL), were developed and validated across 2 vendor bioanalytical laboratories. Plasma samples were processed by simple protein precipitation, and the extracts evaporated to dryness and reconstituted in 0.1% formic acid in water. Chromatographic separation of analytes from endogenous components, and from one another, was effected using a Waters HSS T3 analytical column and detection was performed using tandem mass spectrometry. Method validation was conducted, and met acceptance criteria, according to ICH M10 guidance. Appropriate reference standards were sourced for each analyte and stable isotopically-labelled versions of each analyte were used as internal standards. Suitable conditions for sample handling and storage were assessed, and acceptable stability results were validated. Stability conditions were limited by the facile oxidation of psilocin but plasma samples could be kept thawed on wet ice for 8h or frozen at -80{degrees}C for 6 months, and subjected to 4 freeze/thaw cycles. The validated ranges were shown to be appropriate for the concentrations determined in samples taken in subsequent clinical studies, and data reliability was demonstrated from successful ISR analysis. Comparative performance of the multi-analyte method, across vendor laboratories, was shown through conduct of a cross-validation study employing spiked-QC and incurred samples. HIGHLIGHTSO_LILC-MS/MS methods for quantification of psilocybin, psilocin and major metabolites in human plasma C_LIO_LISummary of validation results for method performance and analyte stability C_LIO_LIApplication of method in a PK study of healthy volunteers and collated ISR analysis results C_LIO_LICross-validation assessment of methods established at 2 bioanalytical vendor laboratories C_LI

items.title: Presynaptic inhibition switches hippocampal mossy fiber computations and limits vesicle pool plasticity
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Science and Technology Austria
items.abstract: Hippocampal mossy fiber synapses act as powerful teacher synapses in CA3 memory networks, yet how their detonation properties are regulated remains unclear. Combining presynaptic and paired recordings, electron and expansion microscopy, and optogenetic stimulation in mouse hippocampal slices, we show that both exogenously applied baclofen and {gamma}-aminobutyric acid (GABA) synaptically released from inhibitory interneurons control transmission and plasticity at hippocampal mossy fiber synapses via presynaptic GABAB receptors. Presynaptic inhibition markedly changes the computational properties of the synapse, switching it from a detonation into a subdetonation mode. Powerful modulation is enabled by a combination of effects on release probability, mediated by the suppression of presynaptic Ca2+ inflow, and on the readily releasable vesicle pool, associated with a reduced number and increased dispersion of docked synaptic vesicles at the ultrastructural level. Synaptically released GABA reverses established post-tetanic potentiation, suggesting interference with vesicle storage mechanisms potentially underlying short-term memory ("vesicle pool engram"). Our results reveal a previously unrecognized inhibitory-excitatory interaction at a central excitatory synapse, in which presynaptic inhibition both sets the computational properties of transmission and limits the persistence of vesicle pool engrams. (181 words) TeaserGABAergic control at mossy fiber synapses tunes detonation and limits vesicle pool plasticity in hippocampal memory circuits

items.title: Non-fatiguing physical exercise induces sustained changes in motor unit discharge patterns and estimated synaptic inputs to motoneurons
items.corresponding_institution: Nantes Université, Movement-Interactions-Performance, MIP, UR 4334, F-44000, Nantes, France.
items.abstract: Non-fatiguing exercise modulates neural excitability in motor pathways controlling both exercised and unexercised muscles. Whether these effects also alter the synaptic control of spinal motoneurons remains unclear. This study investigated how acute non-fatiguing exercise influences motor unit discharge patterns and the estimated contributions of neuromodulatory input and excitation-inhibition balance, depending on muscle activation during exercise. Fourteen participants completed two 30-minute rowing conditions involving either the upper body or the full body. High-density surface electromyography was used to assess tibialis anterior motor unit discharge properties before and up to one hour after exercise. The contributions of neuromodulatory input and excitation-inhibition balance to motor unit discharge were estimated using paired motor unit analysis and geometric characteristics of discharge patterns. At matched torque, peak motor unit discharge rates increased following both exercise conditions, with effects persisting for up to 45 minutes. However, the estimated contributions of synaptic inputs differed between conditions. Following upper-body exercise, when the tibialis anterior was minimally activated, changes in motor unit discharge patterns suggested an enhanced contribution of neuromodulatory input, with no clear changes in excitation-inhibition balance. In contrast, the analyses following full-body exercise suggested a lower contribution of inhibition with respect to excitation, without clear evidence of enhanced neuromodulatory input. These findings suggest that similar increases in motor unit discharge rates following non-fatiguing exercise can be associated with different contributions of synaptic inputs. Overall, our data suggest that acute non-fatiguing exercise induces sustained changes in motor unit discharge patterns, even in muscles minimally involved in the task. The estimated contributions of neuromodulatory input and excitation-inhibition balance to these changes appear to depend on muscle activation during exercise, providing new insights into the neural regulation of spinal motoneuron activity following non-fatiguing exercise.

items.title: EpiState-T for representing epigenetic states across time
items.abstract: Epigenetic information is central to cellular identity, aging and rejuvenation. Unlike the relatively stable genomic sequence shared by most somatic cells, epigenetic states vary across cells and time, making their dynamics difficult to reconstruct from sparse experimental measurements. We introduce EpiState-T, the Temporal Epigenetic State Tensor, to represent selected epigenetic states across intervals and distinguish an observed trajectory from the use of a retained record. In a ten-cell simulation, an explicit reader can act on each cells surviving baseline record. Across 500 paired simulations, mean final distance to the cells own baseline was 0.736 with reading disabled, 0.182 with correctly assigned records and 0.402 with reassigned records. These differences follow from the specified reader. We separately applied the observation and transition tensors to 859,151 CpGs measured in three donor-associated fibroblast cultures before, during and after transient reprogramming. Among sites ending within 0.05 methylation units of baseline, 9.75-15.72% had first departed in treated cultures, compared with 5.37-9.91% in matched mock cultures. The intermediate measurement therefore distinguishes paths that an endpoint comparison merges. These are paths of population measurements: the human data do not track individual cells or establish that cells read a historical record. EpiState-T provides an initial mathematical framework for investigating temporal epigenetic information while keeping state representation, observed change and proposed biological mechanisms distinct.

items.title: Understanding robustness and enabling remediation of neuroimaging-based deep neural networks for digital security: Semantic segmentation of brain tumors as illustrative study
items.corresponding_institution: Neuroimaging Laboratory, Life Sciences Dept, Shiv Nadar University (Institution of Eminence), Delhi NCR, 201314, India; SNU-Dassault Centre of Excellence for Re
items.abstract: BackgroundApplications of deep learning models in neuroimaging have significantly advanced translational neuroscience, offering substantial benefits to human health. However, recent cybersecurity threats have undermined the reliability of digital neuroscience tools, posing challenges to the clinical neuroscience community. A critical issue is the automated semantic segmentation of malignant or premalignant brain tumors, essential for neurosurgery and radiotherapy planning. New methodsThis study investigates the robustness of customary deep learning models such as Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and more recent Vision Transformers (ViTs) in semantic segmentation against adversarial attacks. We assess the performance of CNNs and ViTs under ideal nonhostile conditions and then under cybersecurity threats. ResultsOur findings reveal that while CNNs perform well in ideal conditions, their efficiency sharply declines under adversarial perturbations. In contrast, ViTs maintain their segmentation performance even when subjected to adversarial attacks. This study is the first to apply Visual Transformers for cybersecurity challenge, leveraging advanced capabilities of VITs to enhance robustness against digital perturbations. Comparison with existing methodsCompared to CNNs, which are widely used for neuroimages but vulnerable to adversarial attacks, ViTs demonstrate superior resilience. Our research highlights that ViTs are as effective as CNNs under ideal conditions but offer enhanced protection from cybersecurity angle, making them a more robust choice for neuroimaging applications. ConclusionOur results indicate that for large-scale segmentation operation in neuroimaging, such as lesion segmentation tasks, ViT-based models should be preferred over CNN-based models. This shift could provide inherent protection against prevalent digital threats, ensuring more reliable and secure neuroimaging diagnostics.

items.title: Sex-Related Associations Between Precuneus Volume and Subjective-Objective Memory Discrepancy in Amyloid-Positive Individuals
items.abstract: INTRODUCTIONThe precuneus, a metamemory-related parietal region with sex-specific vulnerability in Alzheimers disease (AD), may contribute to reduced insight of memory deficit. We investigated whether precuneus structural integrity explained sex differences in subjective-objective memory discrepancy. METHODSPrecuneus volumes, as well as three other control regions, were acquired in 350 A{beta}+ and 310 A{beta}-participants from the ADNI dataset to quantify within-individual changes in subjective-objective memory discrepancy across AD progression. RESULTSA{beta}+ participants exhibited steeper objective memory decline ({beta} = -0.446, p < 0.001) despite stable subjective complaints ({beta} = -0.027, p = 0.587), resulting in a widening subjective-objective memory discrepancy ({beta} = 0.317, p < 0.001). In this group, only precuneus atrophy showed a sex-dependent association with discrepancy ({beta} = 0.508, p = 0.002), a finding absent in the A{beta}- group or other brain regions. DISCUSSIONThe precuneus represents a neuroanatomical substrate associated with sex-related differences in metacognitive vulnerability in A{beta}+ individuals.

items.title: Olfactory-Visual Integration Facilitates Scene Perception through Modulation of the Parahippocampal Place Area
items.abstract: Visual scenes anchor our experience of the world, yet the places in which scenes unfold are defined not only by what we see but also by what we smell. Whether and how odors contribute to the neural representation of visual scenes remains poorly understood. Here we asked whether a semantically congruent odor facilitates scene perception and identified the neural mechanisms supporting this facilitation. In two behavioral experiments, participants judged whether briefly presented, masked images depicted intact or scrambled scenes while continuously smelling an odor. A congruent odor lowered the exposure duration needed for accurate scene detection, and a placebo experiment, in which participants merely believed they were smelling an odor, failed to reproduce this benefit, indicating that the facilitation depends on actual sensory input rather than semantic priming. In an fMRI experiment, congruent odors enhanced responses and sharpened category-level scene representations in the parahippocampal place area (PPA), with the congruency-driven enhancement localized to the same anterior subregion that encoded scene identity. A conjunction analysis revealed superadditive responses to congruent odor-scene pairs in the orbitofrontal cortex (OFC) and hippocampus, and psychophysiological interaction analyses showed that congruent stimulation strengthened functional coupling among the OFC, PPA, and piriform cortex. Notably, the piriform cortex decoded visual scene identity after congruent odor-scene pairing, suggesting that odor-scene binding extends scene representations into primary olfactory cortex. Together, these findings identify the PPA as a site where olfactory signals refine the neural code for visual scenes and reveal an OFC-coordinated piriform-OFC-PPA network through which smell shapes our sense of place.

items.title: A Deep Learning Model for Quantifying and Mapping Human Spiral Ganglion Neurons (SGNs): The SGN Base Model
items.abstract: IntroductionSpiral ganglion neurons (SGNs) transmit auditory information and are a histological marker that have been quantified for decades to study various hearing loss pathologies in human temporal bone (hTB) specimens. Historically, quantification of SGNs has been labor-intensive and subject to manual bias and error. With the advent of digital microscopy, this study introduces and assesses the accuracy of a deep learning model for SGN quantification, providing an efficient approach that enables in-depth analysis of SGN distribution through three-dimensional frequency mapping. MethodsDigitized mid-modiolar slides from six hTBs from the Mass Eye and Ear Otopathology Laboratory Collection, representing a range of ages, post-mortem times, and diagnoses, were selected to train a computer vision model. Using Dragonfly 2024.1, the nucleus and cytoplasm of each SGN were manually segmented against background and used as the training corpus. The model was systemically evaluated in eighteen new cases to assess its accuracy across diverse histopathological presentations. For the specimen with the lowest performance, five small regions were manually annotated to augment the training dataset to evaluate the adaptability of the model. Next, the model was applied to every available slide that includes Rosenthals canal for a single case to assess model performance throughout the entire cochlea. Model performance was evaluated by comparing model SGN counts with counts by an experienced investigator, classifying each model prediction as a true positive, false positive, or false negative. Using coordinates output by the model, three-dimensional reconstructions were generated to analyze model performance from base to apex. ResultsA U-Net convolutional neural network was developed with an average Dice coefficient of 0.91. Across eighteen cases representing diverse SGN morphologies and densities, the model achieved an F1-score of 0.91. For the case with the lowest performance, fine-tuning the model by adding additional training data from the same case improved the r2 value from 0.919 to 0.996. When applied to all available slides from a single case, the model achieved an F1-score of 0.96 across the entire cochlea. ConclusionWe present the pretrained SGN Base Model: an approach for quantifying SGNs in hTB specimens that improves efficiency while maintaining high accuracy in comparison to manual quantification. The model performs robustly throughout the cochlea and is adaptable to a diverse range of archival hTB specimens with variable SGN densities and morphologies. Model-generated spatial coordinates for each SGN enable three-dimensional analysis and detailed mapping of SGN density from base to apex.

items.title: Global weight-Ranked cluster-grOWing (GROW): A Cluster-Growing Framework for Robust Functional Coordinate Network Mapping
items.abstract: Coordinate Network Mapping (CNM) has become an important approach for translating scattered neuroimaging findings into circuit-level models of brain disorders such as Alzheimers disease (AD). But conventional CNM uses fixed-radius spheres and pools heterogeneous studies without accounting for confounders. We developed Global weight-Ranked cluster-grOWing (GROW), which reconstructs clusters behind reported peaks using cluster information and a reference statistical weight map, without original imaging data. We analyzed data from 521 participants and 69 published studies (82 experiments, 5,555 participants). GROW-CNM was compared with fixed-radius CNM (Fixed-CNM) in spatial fidelity, cross-study convergence, sampling stability, and sensitivity to confounders. At study level, Fixed-CNM corresponded poorly with the reference atrophy-derived functional network in AD (Spearman r = -0.24, overlap = 1.61%), and radius changes did not improve fidelity. In contrast, GROW-CNM recovered cluster morphology and generated maps closer to the reference network (r [≥] 0.85, overlap [≥] 87.30%). GROW-CNM also showed greater cross-study convergence (median peak probability, 0.99 vs. 0.67; z = 27.42, p < 0.001) and was robust to threshold/resampling (z = -169.84, p < 0.001). Fixed-CNM was associated with systematic factors; GROW-CNM was more sensitive to demographic confounders (p < 0.05, TFCE-FWE correction). Systematic confounding was attenuated by GROW-CNM; Fixed-CNM remained susceptible in core regions (p < 0.001).
