Together, our results provide a resource mapping lipidomic changes across the Alzheimer's risk triad and demonstrate that engineered rLPs can counter lipid accumulation and associated pathology in the brain, and cognitive deficits in vivo.

items.title: Modeling Speech-in-Noise Performance Using an Auditory-Nerve Manifold
items.abstract: Speech-in-noise difficulties often exceed audiometric profile-based predictions, suggesting suprathreshold neural coding deficits limit understanding even when audibility is preserved. A major limitation of clinical speech tests is that reduced performance can reflect either hair-cell loss or cochlear neural degeneration (CND). We propose a computational framework estimating each factor relative contribution at a population level. We simulated auditory-nerve responses to a consonant-identification task for 94 adults (19-83 years; pure-tone average (PTA) 0-55 dB HL) under three conditions: audiometric loss alone, CND affecting low- and medium-spontaneous-rate (LS and MS) fibers, and CND affecting all fiber types. A convolutional autoencoder was used to learn low-dimensional embeddings from neurograms, and downstream classifiers were used to perform consonant identification from the embeddings. We found that audiometric loss alone, and CND of LS and MS fibers consistently produced mismatch between model and human accuracies, whereas CND affecting all fiber types predicted human accuracy closely (mean absolute error (MAE) = 0.089, r = 0.81, rho = 0.83) on an individual level, while capturing the broad structure of human confusions.

items.title: Neuronal heparan sulfate controls the brain accumulation and glymphatic clearance of pathogenic α-synuclein
items.abstract: In Parkinson's disease and dementia with Lewy bodies, fibrillar aggregates of the -synuclein (-syn) protein are released into the extracellular space and drive disease progression, yet the mechanisms governing their in vivo neuronal uptake and clearance remain poorly understood. Heparan sulfate proteoglycans (HSPGs) act as receptors for -syn fibril internalization in iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and could therefore advance synucleinopathy progression in patients. Here we show that -syn fibrils interact electrostatically with the sulfate groups in the HS chains with high affinity, and that genetically reducing the sulfation of neuronal HS reduces the accumulation of -syn aggregates in multiple brain areas, the loss of dopaminergic neurons, and the development of a locomotor behavioral phenotype in mice intracerebrally injected with -syn recombinant fibrils (PFFs). In vivo imaging revealed that HS is also a molecular obstacle to the glymphatic clearance of -syn fibrils, as radiolabeled -syn PFFs travel faster through the brain towards cerebrospinal clearance in mice with less sulfated neuronal HS than in wild-type mice. Collectively, this study provides in vivo evidence that neuronal HS accelerates -syn pathology, potentially by promoting neuronal uptake while slowing the glymphatic clearance of -syn fibrils and, therefore, is a promising therapeutic target to halt synucleinopathies.

items.title: Instruction Timing Governs Representational Competition in Behavioral Timescale Synaptic Plasticity
items.abstract: Neurons can form new representations within a single experience through behavioral-timescale synaptic plasticity (BTSP), yet how such rapid learning affects previously established representations remains unclear. We present an analytically tractable theory of BTSP, constrained by experimental measurements in hippocampal CA1, to examine how successive learning events interact within individual neurons. Competition between temporally narrow potentiation and broader, weight-dependent depression generates nonmonotonic interference as a function of the separation between instructive events. Nearby events merge representations, intermediate separations produce the strongest suppression and overwriting, and distant events allow coexistence. This interference arises from the distinct timescales of potentiation and depression rather than the precise functional form of the plasticity kernel. Analytically derived synaptic-weight covariances identify the origin of this constructive-destructive interaction, and a quantitative phase diagram predicts how the transitions between regimes depend on running speed and the spatial tuning of presynaptic inputs. The theory further identifies a velocity-dependent exclusion zone in which the coexistence of distinct representations is strongly suppressed. The effects of new learning therefore depend not only on the animal's current running speed but also on the pre-existing tuning width of presynaptic inputs. Our theory thus predicts the conditions under which new hippocampal place fields merge with, overwrite, or preserve existing representations.

items.title: One genome, two connectomes: genetic encoding of synapse drive to specify environment-appropriate wiring
items.corresponding_institution: Lunenfeld-Tanenbaum Research Institute, Mount Sinai Hospital, Toronto, ON, Canada
items.abstract: The form of neural wiring must be robust as well as appropriate for the environment. In resource-rich environments, C. elegans larvae rapidly mature into reproductive adults; otherwise, they enter dauer diapause, a state with altered physiology and behaviors for survival and dispersal from harsh environments. By comparing the electron microscopic reconstruction of multiple dauers and non-dauers, we define two consensus connectomes that stereotypically differ in approximately 1/3 wiring partnerships. We show that these wiring differences result from changes in the availability and selectivity of neurite neighbors to form synapses, as well as how strongly wiring partners choose to connect. We further demonstrate that these changes are best quantified by synapse drive, represented as the density of synapses on available contact, and a pair of synapse drive changes have behavioral consequences. We propose that a connectome results from environment-informed genetic specification of synapse drive, the principal determinant of wiring partnership, among available neurite neighbors.

items.title: The degree of Amyloid β pathology determines the impact of autophagy deficiency
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Neurobiology, Care Sciences and Society, Center for Alzheimer Research, Division of Neurogeriatrics, Karolinska Institutet, Stockholm, Sweden
items.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is characterized by amyloid {beta} (A{beta}) deposition, tau aggregation and impaired proteostasis, including autophagy dysfunction. However, how autophagy deficiency affects A{beta} pathology and disease progression remains unclear. We crossed excitatory neuronspecific Atg7 knockout mice with App knock-in mice (AppNL-F/NL-F and AppNL-G-F/NL-G-F) and assessed A{beta} pathology, extracellular vesicle (EV) release, cognition, gamma oscillatory activity, cell death, brain atrophy and proteomic changes. Autophagy deficiency reduced extracellular A{beta} plaque burden despite increased release of A{beta}-containing EVs. Notably, combined Arctic-A{beta} pathology and autophagy deficiency impaired gamma oscillatory activity, behaviour and memory, activated cell death signalling and shortened lifespan. CA1 proteomics identified a voltage-gated potassium channel subunit markedly increased upon Atg7 deletion. Surprisingly, less pronounced A{beta} pathology counteracted several detrimental effects, potentially through improved cellular transport and reduced protein translation. These findings reveal that autophagy regulates A{beta} metabolism and that A{beta} pathology severity determines the consequences of autophagy deficiency, highlighting autophagy modulation as a context-dependent therapeutic target in AD.

items.title: The body as a network, rhythm as the principle: a FREQ-NESS analysis of human movement
items.abstract: Humans spontaneously move together to rhythm, yet how the body organizes its movements is poorly understood and determining which aspects of this organization support interpersonal coordination requires state-of-the-art analysis methods. By applying for the first time Frequency-resolved Network Estimation via Source Separation (FREQ-NESS) to movement data, we reveal a rhythmic architecture of human movement and show how it shapes coordination between individuals. Using full-body motion capture from dancing dyads, we identify a small set of frequency-specific bodily networks whose organization follows a harmonic hierarchy centred on the musical beat. These networks exhibit distinct spatial configurations, revealing how different rhythmic timescales recruit different patterns of bodily movement. Crucially, not all rhythmic networks contribute equally to interpersonal coordination. The beat emerges as a prominent timescale at which bodily organization and social coordination converge. Shared music primarily enhances the temporal alignment of movement dynamics, whereas visual contact additionally promotes similarity in the bodily configurations expressed by partners, with particularly clear effects at the beat. Together, these findings suggest that interpersonal coordination does not arise from rhythmic movement indiscriminately, but from the engagement of specific rhythmic modes within a structured bodily system. By linking the organization of individual movement to coordination between people, our findings establish a framework for understanding how rhythm connects bodily dynamics and social interaction.

items.title: Single-molecule motion profiling reveals direct and indirect effects of PolyQ expansion on huntingtin dynamics and molecular engagement
items.abstract: Huntingtons disease (HD) is caused by CAG expansion in HTT, but how PolyQ expansion alters huntingtin behaviour in human neurons remains unclear. We combined live single-molecule imaging and tracking with transformer-based motion profiling to resolve full-length HTT dynamics in pluripotent hESCs and their derived cortical- and MSN-like neurons. HTT occupied three behavioural states: bound, confined, and exploratory. PolyQ expansion progressively shifted molecules from bound and confined states toward the exploratory state. These effects emerged at shorter PolyQ lengths in MSN-like neurons, and only at 150Q included faster exploratory diffusion and impaired return to stable bound or confined states. Tag-swap experiments showed that mt- HTT imposed similar defects on co-expressed wild-type HTT (wt-HTT), revealing a dominant effect of the HD mutation on wt-HTT dynamics. Loss of HTT (HTT-/-) or expression of mt-HTT also altered kinesin and myosin dynamics, consistent with changes in the intracellular environment of HD cells. Thus, PolyQ-expanded HTT does not merely acquire abnormal dynamics, it leads to a broader disruption of the cytoplasmic environment in which both wt-HTT and molecular motors operate.

items.title: The unfolded protein response in alveolar type II cells is a therapeutic target in ischemia-reperfusion injury and chronic lung allograft rejection
items.abstract: Although lung transplantation is life saving for patients with end-stage lung disease, its long-term outcome is poor owing to an inexorable process of chronic rejection that culminates in chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD) and death or the need for re-transplantation at a median of 6 years post-transplant. Current immunosuppression fails to prevent CLAD, suggesting the existence of alternative pathways not susceptible to these drugs. Lung-directed autoantibodies have been shown to predict CLAD and reduced post-transplant survival. Here, we observed that serum and bronchoalveolar lavage antibodies to GRP78, a master regulator of the unfolded protein response, identified patients at increased risk for CLAD and death. Anti-GRP78 antibodies were associated with upregulation of HSPA5, the gene encoding GRP78, in alveolar type II cells from human lung allografts, and with translocation of GRP78 to the cell surface, a hallmark of the unfolded protein response. Cell surface GRP78 expression was triggered by lung ischemia-reperfusion injury and was also prominent during the development of ischemia-reperfusion injury-augmented chronic rejection in a mouse lung transplant model. Treatment with the chemical chaperones 4-PBA and TUDCA, which are known to ameliorate endoplasmic reticulum stress during the unfolded protein response, reduced both ischemia-reperfusion injury and chronic allograft rejection in vitro and in mice. Taken together, our data implicate alveolar type II cell stress in the pathogenesis of lung ischemia-reperfusion injury and fibrotic chronic lung allograft rejection and suggest that this phenomenon can be targeted for clinical benefit.

items.title: A modular intranasal Nm-nOMV RBD concatemer vaccine induces broad betacoronavirus-neutralizing antibodies
authors: van den Braak, W. J. P.
items.abstract: Betacoronaviruses pose a major threat to human and animal health due to their propensity to cause spillover infections. Broadly protective vaccines that induce mucosal immunity may strengthen pandemic preparedness by limiting infection and onward transmission. Here we have developed intranasal betacoronavirus vaccine candidates combining AdJane Biosciences' Neisseria meningitidis native outer membrane vesicle (Nm-nOMV) platform, a self-adjuvating mucosal delivery platform recently shown to be safe and well tolerated in a first-in-human Phase 1 trial, with multivalent coronavirus spike immunogens. We evaluated betacoronaviruses full Spike proteins, chimeric full Spike proteins, and Receptor Binding Domain (RBD) concatemers representing sarbecoviruses, merbecoviruses, and embecoviruses. Antigenic profiling identified immunogens retaining activity against human convalescent sera and characterized monoclonal antibodies. In mice, intranasal immunization with Nm-nOMVs combined with RBD concatemers induced mucosal IgA responses, systemic IgG and broad neutralization of homologous and heterologous human and bat related betacoronaviruses. Together, findings from the study identify multivalent RBD concatemers co-administered with the Nm-nOMV platform as a promising, modular antigen design for the development of broadly protective mucosal vaccines against emerging betacoronaviruses.

items.title: Human Lung Mast cell Diversity Across Anatomical Compartments Defined by Single-Cell Transcriptomics
items.abstract: Background: Mast cells are key regulators of inflammatory lung diseases, including asthma. Yet, the heterogeneity of lung mast cells and their specialization in different lung compartments remain poorly defined. Traditional protease-based classifications fail to capture distinct mast cell states relevant to airway pathology, highlighting the need for high-resolution, compartment-resolved analyses. Objective: To determine the heterogeneity of human lung mast cells in different lung compartments. Methods: We performed single-cell RNA sequencing analysis of human lung mast cells from four anatomical compartments; bronchi, parenchyma, arteries and veins. Bioinformatical analysis was used to characterize mast cell heterogeneity and compartment-specific specialization. Results: Five transcriptional distinct mast cell states (MC1-MC5) were identified. MC1 was characterized by stress response (e.g., MT2A, MRPL14, SNN), MC2 by broad immediate-early gene activation (e.g., FOS, JUN), and MC3 by a more selective activation with TGF-{beta} response enrichment. MC4 displayed a pro-inflammatory effector phenotype enriched for IL-33-responses (e.g., CCL2, CCL4, CCL4L2, IL13), consistent with roles in airway inflammation. MC5 was associated with long non-coding RNAs (MEG3, MEG8). Mast cell states showed anatomical segregation with inflammatory cytokines enriched in bronchial and arterial mast cells while reduced in parenchymal mast cells. We further identified MCTC-like mast cells co-expressing CTSG, CMA1 and ADCYAP1, characterized by enhanced metabolic programming. Conclusions: This study provides a comprehensive single-cell transcriptomic atlas of human lung mast cells, revealing five distinct transcriptional states and compartment-specific functional specialization. These findings link mast cell heterogeneity to airway inflammation and provide a translational framework for targeting mast cells in lung diseases.

items.title: Whole-blood and PBMC-based assays reveal hidden inflammatory responses to decellularized materials for heart valve replacement
items.corresponding_institution: Institute of Experimental Haematology and Transfusion Medicine, , University Hospital Bonn, University of Bonn, Bonn, Germany
items.abstract: Reliable assessment of inflammatory activity is essential for the development of biological heart valve materials. However, the responses detected depend critically on the assay system. Following inconsistent and weak responses in standard macrophage assays, we systematically compared human whole blood with isolated immune-cell models to evaluate laboratory-prepared decellularized aortic valves from human donors and clinically used biological valve materials. The laboratory-prepared valves underwent histological and biochemical characterization and were prepared using the same protocol used for ovine aortic valves transplanted in vivo. They induced pronounced proinflammatory responses in whole blood and peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs) compared with clinical valve prostheses, whereas macrophages and THP-1 cells showed little cytokine release for any of the materials. Surface coating was associated with lower levels of selected cytokines but did not eliminate inflammatory activity. PBMCs readily detected proinflammatory activity, while whole blood revealed additional response patterns. In whole blood, fixed bovine and porcine pericardium induced higher expression of selected proinflammatory genes than decellularized human aortic valve tissue. Median IFN-2 concentrations were highest with the human valve tissue. These findings demonstrate that material characterization does not replace functional assessment of inflammatory activity and that assay selection determines which aspects of the response are captured. PBMC and whole-blood testing provide complementary functional approaches for comparing material preparations. Together, these assays support the evaluation of tissue processing and surface modification in biological heart valve development.

items.title: High-resolution cryo-EM of ribosomes in mammalian neurons
items.corresponding_institution: RNA Therapeutics Institute, UMass Chan Medical School, 368 Plantation Street, Worcester, MA 01605, USA
items.abstract: Brain function depends on protein synthesis (translation), which controls neurodevelopment, synaptic plasticity, and memory formation. To understand the molecular mechanisms of translational control, the functional states of neuronal ribosomes must be determined. We visualized the translational apparatus within induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived human neurons and in human and mouse neuron-derived lysates, using cryogenic electron microscopy (cryo-EM) with high-resolution 2D template matching (2DTM) and large-area imaging (DeCo-LACE). Cryo-EM maps at up to 2.6 [A] resolution reveal structural details of numerous functional states of ribosomes. Initiating 40S subunits abundantly feature initiation factor eIF1S (also known as 5MP) indicating a tight control of translation initiation. Ribosomes with elongation factors comprise ~90% of 80S particles, suggesting a high prevalence of translating ribosomes. Most elongating ribosomes sample pre-decoding states with aminoacyl-tRNA*eEF1A*GTP and a well-resolved decoding center prior to aminoacyl-tRNA acceptance. On the large ribosomal subunit, a conserved loop of uL16 stabilizes the CCA end of peptidyl-tRNA, suggesting a ribosomal protein contribution into RNA-catalyzed peptidyl transfer. The composition of peripheral ribosomal proteins, including the P-stalk proteins proposed to be substoichiometric in neurons, is homogeneous throughout ribosome states. The compositional heterogeneity of ribosomes is therefore negligible or only occurs under specific cellular conditions. Our work provides a comprehensive visualization of ribosome states within neurons and paves the way for probing translation regulation and dysregulation in neurological diseases using cryo-EM.

items.title: Reference genomes for Australian Cryptosporidium hominis and C. parvum from humans
items.abstract: Cryptosporidium hominis and C. parvum are important protozoan pathogens of humans worldwide, and genomic surveillance is increasingly being used to investigate transmission and outbreaks. However, no complete Cryptosporidium genome is available from Australia, and many common Cryptosporidium gp60 subtypes lack high-quality genome assemblies worldwide. This study generated the first Australian reference genomes for two clinically relevant, zoonotic Cryptosporidium species, C. hominis and C. parvum from human hosts, as well as a scaffold-level genome for Australian C. meleagridis. Oocysts were purified from eleven clinical faecal samples and whole-genome sequencing was performed using short-read technologies. Three samples belonging to different species were also sequenced using long-read technology, with assemblies generated, telomere recovery undertaken and genomes annotated. High-quality reference C. hominis IaA12R3 genome (8 T2T chromosomes, 9.2 Mb, 4069 genes, 98.4% completeness), near-complete C. parvum IIaA20G3R1 genome (8 chromosomes, 9.2 Mb, 4004 genes, 98.2% completeness), and a draft C. meleagridis IIIgA31 genome (113 scaffolds, 9.3 Mb, 4075 genes, 97.2% completeness) were generated and had high nucleotide similarity (98-99%), gene cluster orthology (99%) and genome synteny relative to available international reference genomes. Phylogenomic analyses with global C. hominis and C. parvum genomes were performed to characterise the relationships of Australian isolates globally showing Australian C. hominis and C. parvum forming well-supported clades with North American European isolates. Whole-genome analyses of eight Australian C. hominis isolates revealed markedly better resolution of genetic relationships than gp60 subtyping alone. This study provides the resources for national genomic surveillance in Australia and expands the genomic representation of clinically relevant Cryptosporidium subtypes. Broader application of genomic surveillance has the potential to enhance outbreak investigation, improve understanding of transmission dynamics and support One Health approaches to cryptosporidiosis control.

items.title: A Benchmark for Generative Modeling of High-Dimensional Enzyme Kinetic Parameters of Metabolic Networks
items.abstract: Large-scale kinetic models predict how metabolism responds to genetic and environmental perturbations, but building them at scale is limited by the scarcity of experimentally determined enzyme kinetic parameters. Generative machine learning has been proposed to address this bottleneck, yet prior work has each introduced a single, bespoke architecture, leaving open which generative paradigm suits this problem and why. We introduce a benchmark suite for generative modeling of high-dimensional enzyme kinetic parameter sets: labeled datasets of kinetically feasible Escherichia coli models paired with a mechanistically grounded evaluation harness that scores generated ensembles on dynamical stability and agreement with experimentally observed phenotypes, rather than statistical realism alone. Using it, we compare three standard architectures at matched capacity, a conditional variational autoencoder, a Wasserstein GAN with gradient penalty, and a RealNVP normalizing flow, each under two conditioning schemes (a discrete high/low label and a continuous, graded key-performance-indicator target), across a difficulty ladder from one mutant phenotype to a stringent class of nine reproduced jointly. Two findings stand out. The architectures trace a consistent concentration-exploration trade-off, the VAE concentrating, the flow exploring and extrapolating, the GAN in between, but this ordering is overturned at high stringency by the conditioning scheme: at the joint class, continuous targets reach 33 to 117-fold enrichment over random sampling for every architecture, whereas discrete labels stay at 1.3 to 15-fold. Beyond the comparison, the suite is an accessible, mechanistically validated reference task for groups outside the kinetic-modeling community to benchmark their own generative algorithms.

items.title: EHRMENEIA: A Benchmark for Foundation Models on Longitudinal Electronic Health Records
items.abstract: Electronic health record foundation models are evaluated using heterogeneous targets, vocabularies, and adaptation procedures, preventing systematic characterization across model families. We introduce EHRMENEIA (https://ehrmeneia.upc.edu/), a benchmark that provides a multidimensional evaluation framework for next-event prediction, multi-horizon event occurrence, trajectory fidelity and few-shot representation transfer. EHRMENEIA preserves each model's native vocabulary and temporal representation while mapping clinical outputs to shared evaluation objects. Applied to two released clinical checkpoints and two synthetic demonstrations, the framework exposed substantial differences not only in performance but in the clinical questions that could be evaluated from each model--dataset interface. EHRMENEIA introduces a view of benchmarking in which the supported clinical evaluation domain is identified before performance within that domain is interpreted. The framework therefore shifts foundation-model benchmarking from scalar ranking toward characterization of what can, and cannot, be inferred from model outputs.

items.title: Task-aligned foundation model representations enable single-cell cytokine response inference
items.corresponding_institution: Pohang University of Science and Technology (POSTECH)
items.abstract: Inferring cellular responses from single-cell transcriptomes requires interpreting changes relative to an appropriate baseline while retaining cell-type context. Here we present CYTAP, which adapts frozen single-cell foundation model embeddings for cytokine-response inference by combining donor-adjusted receiver states with deviations from matched control centroids. CYTAP uses a shared classifier to assign relative single-cell response scores across 90 cytokines and supports unpaired analyses using counterfactual control references. Baseline-relative representations improved held-out-donor prediction with both State SE and scFoundation. Across independent perturbation datasets, CYTAP prioritized applied cytokines, including when receptor transcripts were sparsely detected, and ranked administered cytokines among the top ten in both in vivo datasets. In an unpaired COVID-19 cohort, inferred responses were associated with severity, and IL-6 response scores correlated with plasma IL-6 concentrations. These findings support the use of biologically defined references to adapt pretrained representations for functional response inference.

items.title: GNEval: A Context-Specific Benchmark for Gene Network Inference with Single-Cell Foundation Models
items.abstract: Gene network (GN) inference plays a critical role in understanding gene relationships and their roles in biological functions and diseases. Existing single-cell GN inference methods often rely on limited data from individual studies. Single-cell foundation models, pretrained on large and diverse datasets, provide a range of gene-gene association signals that offer a promising basis for GN inference. However, it remains unclear which GN properties these signals capture and how they compare with domain-specific methods. To address this gap, we introduce GNEval, a unified benchmark for evaluating pretrained model derived gene associations for network inference. We benchmark 21 gene representations and association scores from 11 models, including static gene embeddings (S), contextual embeddings (C), and gene-gene attention scores (A). GNEval assesses inferred networks based on their consistency with functional and perturbational evidence, including 14 Perturb-seq datasets across diverse cell systems, perturbation types and data sizes. The results reveal substantial heterogeneity across evaluation tasks and models. Rankings based on Gene Ontology and Perturb-seq evidence were nearly uncorrelated (Spearman {rho} = -0.05). Context-independent representations showed a substantial advantage in recovering functional relationships ({Delta}AUROC = 0.13), whereas context-dependent gene associations improved recovery of perturbation-associated differential expression relationships by 3.8x. The domain-specific method achieves relatively strong performance on both evidence types, offering a better balance across the two evaluations than most foundation-model-derived networks. Overall, gene representations and association scores show task-specific strengths, highlighting the need for task-aware selection and integration with domain-specific methods.

items.title: CellTouch: Learning to separate touching nuclei in anisotropic 3D cell cultures
items.abstract: 3D-oids, such as spheroids and organoids, are essential models in drug discovery and precision medicine, and quantitative analysis requires every nucleus to be segmented separately. Accurate 3D instance segmentation remains challenging, because nuclei are densely packed and touching, and volumes are sampled more coarsely along the Z-axis than laterally. Most existing methods were developed for near-isotropic data and tend to merge neighbouring nuclei. To address this challenge, we propose CellTouch, a deep learning method for anisotropic 3D nuclei instance segmentation that predicts flow fields and a contact channel, which separates touching nuclei directly from the network output. Ablations showed that the contact channel is the key design element, and CellTouch outperformed state-of-the-art methods on in-house data and widely used public datasets. Most importantly, dense Z-sampling is not required: CellTouch segmented nuclei as accurately at a 2 um Z-step as at 0.5 um, reducing acquisition time and data volume four-fold.

items.title: Characterization of Natural Killer Cell-Associated Prognostic Signature Reveals Immune Landscape and Prognostic Value in Uterine Corpus Endometrial Carcinoma (UCEC)
items.abstract: Background: Natural killer (NK) cells are critical in eliminating virus-infected and cancer cells. Uterine corpus endometrial carcinoma (UCEC) is a common malignancy in women, and the role of NK cells in UCEC has attracted significant attention. This study aims to develop an NK cell-related gene signature (NRGs) to improve immunotherapy response and prognosis evaluation in UCEC. Methods: Consensus clustering classified UCEC samples based on NRGs. Univariate Cox regression, differential expression, and Lasso regression were used to build a prognostic model. Differences in tumor microenvironment (TME), immune checkpoints, and clinical features were compared between high- and low-risk groups. Results: High NK cell infiltration was associated with a favorable prognosis. Eleven key NRGs were identified, and consensus clustering divided patients into two clusters: Cluster 1 (C1) had better prognosis and higher immune cell infiltration. A nine-NRG signature (CEACAM1, IFNG, PTPN6, KNSTRN, XCL1, IL2RG, RAC3, MICB, CCL3) was developed. The high-risk group had more advanced-stage cases, higher-grade tumors, and serous carcinoma compared to the low-risk group (P < 0.05). Conclusions: The 9-NRGs signature demonstrates strong predictive performance and offers valuable insights for future immuno-oncology research.

items.title: Disrupting translation in CA1 pyramidal cells blocks novelty-induced increases in population firing rate while preserving newly formed assemblies
items.abstract: Long-term memory depends upon the translation of the plasticity-related proteins required for synaptic consolidation. Whether learning-related changes in hippocampal CA1 coding and synchrony require local synaptic consolidation or reflect plasticity elsewhere remains unknown. We used the inducible protein kinase R (iPKR) chemogenetic system to downregulate cap-dependent translation in CaMKII-expressing dorsal CA1 neurons through intracerebral infusion of an actuator that activates the integrated stress response. Without chemogenetic activation, iPKR mice exhibited elevated pyramidal cell firing and reduced interneuron firing relative to wild-type mice. Infusion of the chemogenetic actuator suppressed c-Fos expression for at least 24 hours and blocked the novelty-related increase in firing observed following vehicle infusion. Nevertheless, other aspects of experience-dependent physiology persisted. Pyramidal cells active during novel exploration remained preferentially recruited into sharp-wave ripples (SPW-Rs) hours into a post-exposure consolidation period. Pairwise coincident activity patterns formed during novel exploration were also reactivated during SPW-Rs with magnitudes and temporal persistence comparable to vehicle sessions and wild-type mice without infusions. When mice returned five hours after exposure to a novel environment, the assemblies formed during translation disruption were also re-expressed at magnitudes comparable to those observed during repeated familiar-environment visits and following novel exploration under vehicle. These findings demonstrate that experience-dependent reorganization of CA1 pyramidal cell synchrony can survive disruption of plasticity-related protein production, whereas novelty-related changes in excitability are impaired. Therefore, SPW-R reactivation and cell assembly consolidation likely depend upon plasticity pathways outside of the eIF2-dependent signaling pathways in the CA1 pyramidal cells targeted by the iPKR system.

items.title: Complex IV Subunit C15orf48 Integrates Electron Transport Chain Function with Amino Acid and Lipid Metabolism to Regulate Innate Immunity
items.abstract: Despite extensive recognition of immunometabolism in innate immune regulation, how mitochondrial bioenergetic and metabolic pathways in monocytes interface to control inflammatory responses remains poorly understood. Here, we uncover that C15orf48 (MOCCI/NMES1/COXFA4L3), an inflammation-associated mitochondrial complex IV (CIV) subunit, orchestrates electron transport chain (ETC) function, fatty acid oxidation (FAO), and branched-chain amino acid (BCAA) catabolism to control monocyte activation. Loss of C15orf48 globally and in monocytes confers host tolerance and resistance to bacterial pneumonia and LPS-induced endotoxemia, characterized by reduced inflammatory gene expression, cytokine secretion, and monocyte activation. Mechanistically, C15orf48 increases mitochondrial ROS production and maintains NAD pools, which in turn supports long-chain FAO and BCAA catabolism required for robust monocyte activation and inflammatory cytokine production. These findings define a mitochondrial CIV metabolic axis directed by C15orf48 as central to monocyte activation and innate immunity, filling a key knowledge gap in immunometabolic control and presenting new targets for therapy in infection and sepsis.

items.title: Dual-loop DogTag engineering enables modular antigen display on human vault nanoparticles
items.corresponding_institution: Izmir Biomedicine and Genome Center, VLP Technology Vaccine and Drug Inc.
items.abstract: Self-assembling protein nanoparticles can enhance immune responses by displaying multiple copies of an antigen on their surface. Most previous studies using vault nanoparticles have focused on loading proteins inside the particle or modifying its ends. Here, we introduced two DogTag peptides into separate surface-exposed loops of human major vault protein (MVP), creating up to 156 potential attachment sites on each 78-subunit vault. The engineered MVP formed vault-sized particles in suspension HEK cells, to which separately produced, stabilized influenza H5N1 Clade 2.3.4.4b hemagglutinin (HA) fused to DogCatcher was covalently attached. By varying the amount of HA added, we obtained preparations with estimated loadings of approximately 32, 64, and 124 HA trimers per vault. Structural models showed that increasing HA loading reduced the median distance between neighboring HA trimers from 13.3 to 8.8 nm, while electron microscopy showed that highly loaded particles retained their characteristic vault morphology. Following subcutaneous priming and intranasal boosting in mice, highly loaded HA-decorated vaults induced significantly higher HA-specific serum IgG, IgG1, IgG2a, and IgA titers than soluble HA. Covalent attachment of HA to vaults also resulted in significantly higher IgG2a titers than the non-conjugated mixture of vaults and HA, reaching levels similar to those induced by CpG-adjuvanted HA. Despite the strong HA-specific antibody responses, anti-vault IgG titers remained low. Our approach adds high-density, adjustable antigen display to the established cargo-loading and targeting capabilities of human vaults, offering the possibility of combining all three functions in a single vaccine particle.

items.title: Rare Epithelial Sentinel Cells Establish Functional Domains of the Airway
items.abstract: Organs exposed to the environment must sense threats in order to evoke protective physiologic responses. Recent single-cell sequencing studies of the airway epithelium have led to the identification of a suite of rare epithelial cells, many of which are unified by their ability to sense stimuli1,2. Herein, we explore how organized networks of epithelial sentinel cells transduce distinct stimuli to alter tissue function by employing a combination of cell type-specific calcium indicators, optogenetics, chemogenetics, cell ablation, and live ACh and ATP sensors. We define a new diversity of functional sentinel cells including 3 new subtypes of chemosensory tuft cells. We further show that solitary neuroendocrine cells, like their tuft cell counterparts, generate stimulus-induced waves of calcium activation. These waves originate from a central sentinel cell and expand outwards to encompass a circular domain of surrounding epithelial cells. We demonstrate that basolateral secretion and diffusion of neurotransmitters cause the activation of the surrounding epithelial effector cells including basal stem cells which were not previously known to be participants in sentinel cell-induced calcium waves. We show that these diffusion-limited domains (DLDs) are generated by specific patterns of ACh and ATP secretion characteristic of specific sentinel cell populations. The speed, intensity, and domain size of DLDs are dictated by the degree of stimulus-triggered neurotransmitter secretion. Thus, DLDs represent a unified mechanism for specifying functional domains within the airway epithelium. Triggered sentinel cells generate surrounding circular domains of increased mucociliary transport and enhance stem cell replication. Insulated sentinel cell networks are tuned to distinct stimuli. Sentinel cells are distributed in sufficient numbers to ensure comprehensive epithelial coverage. However, the amplitude and number of DLDs scale with stimulus intensity, permitting both local and global physiologic activation of the epithelium. Additionally, the distribution of sentinel cells can vary with organ anatomy, resulting in compartmentalized physiologic responses. Furthermore, cytokines modulate DLD responses. IL-1{beta} amplifies ciliary action by generating larger and more intense DLDs, while IFN-{gamma} reduces the density of DLDs by directly depleting sentinel cells. Finally, we show that a fungal metabolite triggers DLDs. In aggregate, we reveal a sophisticated collective of diverse sentinel cells that activate surrounding circular domains of airway epithelium to generate protective responses to environmental threats.

items.title: Transient telomerase mRNA delivery extends the proliferative capacity of patient-derived Duchenne muscular dystrophy myogenic progenitors
items.abstract: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) is an X-linked disease, characterised by progressive skeletal and cardiac muscle degeneration and impaired regeneration. Repeated regenerative cycles contribute to muscle stem cell exhaustion, potentially driven by telomere shortening under chronic proliferative demand. Here, we tested whether transient delivery of hTERT mRNA can increase the relative telomere signal (Q-FISH) in patient-derived DMD myogenic progenitors (CD56+) and interstitial (CD56-) cells from two DMD donors, compared with one control donor. hTERT mRNA treatment increased the relative telomere signal and added 2 to 6 population doublings in DMD myogenic progenitors, whereas healthy donor cells showed no comparable benefit in proliferation. Exploratory transcriptomic analysis indicated genotype-associated differences in translation- and cell-cycle-related gene sets following hTERT treatment. Telomere elongation and improved proliferation were not accompanied by recovery of myogenic differentiation; no karyotypic abnormalities were detected under the conditions tested. By transiently increasing the proliferative output of dystrophic cells without genomic integration, this proof of concept provides a basis for further investigation of telomere-associated proliferative limits in DMD and a starting point for future regenerative approaches.

items.title: Chromosome-level genome assembly of the hydrozoan jellyfish Cladonema pacificum
items.abstract: The hydrozoan jellyfish Cladonema pacificum, which possesses experimentally tractable polyp and medusa stages, is an emerging cnidarian model for studies of regeneration, development, physiology, and behavior. Although experimental techniques have been established for this species, the lack of a chromosome-level reference genome has limited genome-wide and comparative analyses. Here, we present the first chromosome-level genome assembly of C. pacificum generated using HiFi long-read sequencing and Hi-C technology. The representative haploid assembly comprises 15 chromosome-scale scaffolds and 121 additional scaffolds, spanning 504.0 Mb with a scaffold N50 of 32.1 Mb. Gene annotation integrating RNA-seq, PacBio Iso-Seq, and protein homology identified 17,206 protein-coding genes, of which 95.7% received at least one functional annotation. Phylogenomic and macrosynteny analyses further confirmed the placement of C. pacificum within Hydrozoa and revealed extensive chromosome-scale conservation with other hydrozoan genomes. This genomic resource provides a valuable foundation for comparative genomics and future molecular, cellular, and evolutionary studies using C. pacificum as an emerging hydrozoan model.

items.title: StarCrew: A pipeline for exploratory analysis of Starship cargo
items.corresponding_institution: Systematic Biology, Department of Organismal Biology, Uppsala University, Uppsala, 752 36, Sweden
items.abstract: BackgroundStarships are giant cargo-mobilizing mobile elements within the fungal subphylum Pezizomycotina that harbor diverse gene content, including genes for virulence and heavy metal resistance. Although Starship elements carry a vast array of cargo genes, the overall composition and function of this cargo remain largely uncharacterized for most elements. While existing bioinformatic tools have been designed for the identification of these elements, a gap remains in tools for characterizing their gene content while accounting for its specific characteristics. ResultsTo address the gap in gene content analysis of Starships, we present StarCrew, a bash- based pipeline designed for systematically characterizing the cargo gene diversity and turnover within Starship elements. We demonstrate that StarCrew robustly handles datasets of varying diversity, providing the capacity to cluster elements based on collinear regions, identify nested insertion events, perform element classification, and highlight overrepresented genes within a dataset. Additionally, StarCrew serves as a diagnostic tool to flag elements requiring boundary curation. We found that the accuracy of the pipeline was sensitive to the quality of input gene models and the precision of initial element boundaries delineation. Demonstrating its utility, we identified a putative pseudokinase as a new conserved protein distributed across Starships. ConclusionsStarCrew provides a practical and versatile resource for the continuous exploration of Starship gene content, designed to adapt alongside our expanding understanding of these mobile elements. Finally, we propose a complementary system to group elements with potential shared beneficial traits, based on collinear blocks, called Functional Constellations.

items.title: Standard benchmarking inflates gene-prioritization accuracy estimates
items.abstract: Benchmark results tell clinics which gene-prioritization system to trust and the field what counts as progress. Standard benchmarking practice --- testing each system using its latest knowledge databases --- can inflate system accuracy estimates and invite data leakage. We formalize the Fairbench protocol: testing may use only knowledge available strictly before the patient's assessment. Against prepublication snapshots dated by case report, on one public case collection, standard benchmarking inflated Top-1 accuracy by 40.5--80.5 percentage points across Exomiser, LIRICAL, Phrank and Phen2Disease. In every system, over half the tested patients had a causal-gene phenotype association whose only recorded source was their case publication. Reassessing three systems' published benchmarks with reproduced or reconstructed references showed the same direction in all five comparisons. Retesting undiagnosed patients with the latest knowledge database is good care. But benchmark results are read as performance at the patient's assessment, and Fairbench is a necessary data-hygiene condition for that reading.

items.title: Distance-stratified benchmarking of variant-effect predictors on β-lactamase deep mutational scanning data
items.abstract: Mutations far from the active site of antibiotic-resistance enzymes can change resistance, but it is unclear what information predicts their effects. We asked how the performance of a protein language model (ESM2), a structure-based stability predictor (ThermoMPNN) and simple structural descriptors changes with distance from the catalytic residues, using deep mutational scanning data for the {beta}-lactamases TEM-1 (four assays) and VIM-2 (one assay). We measured Spearman correlation and AUROC within distance bins, with bootstrap intervals over positions. In TEM-1, ESM2 accuracy fell with distance (Stiffler assay: {rho} = 0.72 below 8 [A] and 0.42 beyond 20 [A]), while the stability score rose ({rho} = 0.41 to 0.70). Adding stability to a model of ESM2, solvent accessibility and neighbour count improved cross-validated {rho} by 0.02 below 8 [A] and 0.10 beyond 20 [A], and the combined model did not decline with distance. The pattern held across binning schemes, in a continuous-distance model, and when any one of five contiguous distal stretches was removed. Two TEM-1 assays are nearly duplicates, and the Deng assay was too noisy to be informative. VIM-2 has only seven positions beyond 20 [A] and showed no detectable trend within 20 [A], so it neither supports nor contradicts the TEM-1 pattern. Nine distal TEM-1 positions remained more sensitive than the models predicted. In TEM-1, predicted stability was more informative than the language model far from the catalytic site, and the language model was stronger near it. Distance-stratified reporting could add to variant-effect benchmarks. The study is exploratory and uses one structure and one phenotype per assay.

items.title: Input Construction Accounts for Most PoseBusters Clash Failures on RNA-Ligand Complexes
items.abstract: PoseBusters, a widely used test of the physical validity of ligand poses, was calibrated on protein-ligand crystal structures, and whether its checks transfer to RNA has not been measured. Applied without filtering the input to 2,970 deposited RNA-ligand poses, the receptor-clash check failed 527 of 2,931 (18.0%), and all but 7 of the failures were in covalently bonded nucleotides or in entries that contain protein, were solved by cryo-electron microscopy or were resolved at worse than 2.0 [A], so most failures are associated with which structures and ligand records entered the input set. On a high-resolution set constructed after these failures were attributed, the check failed 3 of 149 (2.01%; 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.00-4.58%) against 0.32% for the protein benchmark, a difference this set cannot resolve, and the PoseBusters calibration rule selected a threshold of 0.735 against the shipped 0.75. We give a seven-step dataset construction protocol and a tool, rnaprep, that implements its first four steps. On 139 redocking targets, with accuracy measured in the crystal frame without superposition, requiring a valid pose cost NucleoDock 25.2 points (69.06% to 43.88% within 2 [A]) and AutoDock Vina none, and cut the lead of NucleoDock from 38.9 points (95% CI 26.5-50.0) to 13.7 points, a lead not clearly distinguishable from zero (95% CI 1.3-27.5; cluster permutation P = 0.053). For these two programs in one redocking regime, the result supports reporting validity alongside RMSD in RNA docking benchmarks.

items.title: Stromal mitochondrial reprogramming and transfer reveal a chemotherapy-associated tumor state in ovarian cancer
items.abstract: Mitochondrial transfer from stromal cells promotes ovarian cancer progression, yet the functional state of donor mitochondria remains poorly understood. Here we define a stress-adapted mitochondrial state in carcinoma-associated mesenchymal stem cells (CA-MSCs), characterized by increased respiratory and glycolytic activity despite increased mitochondrial proton leak and inefficient coupling of respiration to ATP production, oxidative stress, and elevated mitochondrial DNA variant burden. We identify WT1 as a regulator of mitochondrial reprogramming and PDK4 as a metabolic adaptation critical for CA-MSC growth. We further show that CA-MSCs preferentially transfer highly oxidized mitochondria to ovarian cancer cells. In a freshly-dissociated primary high grade serous ovarian cancer patient tumor, using mitochondrial variant tracking, we identify a transcriptionally distinct tumor population sharing mitochondrial variant patterns with stroma, in line with stromal-tumor mitochondrial transfer. This transcriptional signature is enriched in residual tumors following chemotherapy across four independent patient cohorts. Together, these findings establish stromal mitochondrial reprogramming and the preferential transfer of oxidatively-stressed mitochondria as important features of ovarian cancer heterogeneity and persistence following chemotherapy.

items.title: Alpha-synuclein overexpression induces sex-dependent alterations in striatal autophagic-lysosomal markers in a Parkinson's disease mouse model
items.abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is characterized by pathological alpha-synuclein (-syn) accumulation and alterations in autophagy. While biological sex is increasingly recognized as a modifier of PD susceptibility and pathophysiology, its relationship with striatal autophagic-lysosomal alterations remains incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated sex-dependent changes in related molecular markers in a mouse model overexpressing -syn. Male and female C57BL/6J mice received bilateral intranigral injections of adeno-associated viral vectors encoding mutant A53T -syn or empty vectors. Dorsal striatal tissue from 29 animals was analyzed at 60 or 120 days post-injection. Confocal imaging of LC3B (microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 beta; autophagosome marker) and LAMP1 (lysosomal-associated membrane protein 1; lysosomal marker) immunofluorescence quantified marker-positive areas, puncta densities, and colocalization. Associations with -syn immunoreactivity, striatal dopaminergic innervation, and axonopathy severity were also examined. At 60 days, no vector-related differences in autophagic-lysosomal markers were detected. However, at 120 days, vector x sex interactions were identified for LC3-positive area, LAMP1-positive area, and LC3 puncta density. Post-hoc comparisons showed reductions in all three measures in -syn males relative to male controls, whereas the corresponding comparisons in females were not significant. After adjustment for striatal -syn immunoreactivity, -syn males had lower LC3- and LAMP1-positive areas, LC3-LAMP1 colocalization area, and LAMP1 puncta density than -syn females. Across -syn mice, greater LAMP1 puncta density was associated with more advanced axonopathy after adjustment for sex and time. These findings identify sex-dependent alterations in striatal autophagic-lysosomal markers following A53T -syn overexpression and suggest an association between lysosomal organization and axonopathy severity. They also underscore the importance of considering biological sex in studies of PD pathophysiology and when evaluating therapies targeting protein clearance pathways.

items.title: TAOK1 restrains cerebral cortex size and determines neural progenitor fate through YAP1 suppression
items.corresponding_institution: University of Washington School of Medicine, Seattle
items.abstract: The size and complexity of the human cerebral cortex results from precisely coordinated neural progenitor expansion, differentiation, and fate trajectories for which the controlling molecular programs are not well understood. Pathogenic missense and deletion variants in the protein kinase TAOK1 cause a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability and macrocephaly. We generated human cortical organoids harboring catalytically-inactive TAOK1 disease variant and utilized quantitative phosphoproteomics along with single-cell transcriptomics to uncover disease mechanisms. Catalytically-inactive TAOK1 increases neural progenitor proliferation, accelerates cortical organoid growth, and alters the diversity of cortical cell-types. Phosphoproteomic analyses revealed impaired Hippo signaling with reduced inhibitory phosphorylation of YAP1 concomitant with its sustained nuclear accumulation and activation of TEAD dependent transcription. Progenitors derived from a patient with heterozygous TAOK1 deletion also accumulate nuclear YAP1, extending this finding to a distinct clinical disease-associated TAOK1 lesion. Single-cell transcriptomics demonstrate premature emergence of astrocytic and inhibitory neuronal populations in mutant organoids. Pharmacological inhibition of YAP-TEAD signaling reduced cyclin-A2 labeling and suppressed perturbed Hippo pathway targets. These findings identify TAOK1 as a molecular brake on human cortical overgrowth, implicate previously unrecognized role for Hippo dysfunction in macrocephaly, and reveal pathogenic consequences of accelerated progenitor cycling for both progenitor expansion and fate.

items.title: The temporal dynamics of same vs. different relational integration in the adult brain
items.corresponding_institution: The MARCS Institute for Brain, Behaviour & Development, Western Sydney University
items.abstract: Humans readily abstract common relations across situations that look entirely different. For example, when reading a map, we align relations between landmarks on a screen with those in the world around us. Relational comparison forms the basis of analogical reasoning. Here, we investigated how recognising same and different relations instantiated by various simple shapes unfolds in the brain over time. We recorded EEG from adults (N = 20) viewing shape pairs presented in a periodic visual oddball paradigm, in which exemplars of one relation occurred at regular intervals within a stream of the other (e.g., same-same-same-different or vice versa). Frequency-domain analysis revealed robust responses at the stimulation rate (2.5 Hz) and the oddball rate (0.625 Hz), providing an implicit neural measure of relational discrimination. Time-resolved decoding showed that same and different could be decoded while holding Sequence Role constant: relation decoding was reliable when both relations served as oddballs, but significantly weaker when they served as standards. Same/different decoding at the oddballs generalised to shapes and colours withheld from classifier training and was not explained by stimulus familiarity. These findings show that the brain implicitly registers same and different relations at an abstract level that generalises across different instantiations of these relations, and that this information is expressed most strongly when a given relation differs from its established context.

items.title: Mucosal B Cell Aggregates are Associated with Non-response to JAK1 Inhibitor Therapy in Ulcerative Colitis
items.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory bowel disease with considerable interindividual variation in treatment response and limited efficacy of available therapies in some patients. Predicting individual responses is therefore essential for personalized treatment selection. Filgotinib, a preferential JAK1 inhibitor, induces clinical remission in approximately 40% of patients after 1 year, but mechanisms underlying response remain unclear. Using 38-marker imaging mass cytometry, and immunohistochemistry, we profiled paired colonic biopsies from 25 UC patients before and during filgotinib treatment. Full response (n=8) was defined as an endoscopic Mayo score of 0 at the biopsy site after ten weeks of treatment, while non-response (n=6) was defined as no score improvement at the biopsy site. At baseline, despite comparable inflammation and JAK/STAT activity, full responders showed greater epithelial abundance, whereas non-responders had more B cells. In non-responders, B cells were also more frequently organized into lymphoid aggregates containing ICOS+ CD4 memory and CD57+ CD8 memory T cells. Abundance of these B cell-rich aggregates correlated negatively with lamina propria pJAK1 abundance. This suggests that inflammation driven by these lymphoid aggregates may be relatively JAK1-independent and could therefore contribute to filgotinib non-response. After 10 weeks, neutrophils and HLA-DR+ epithelial cells had decreased more in full responders than in non-responders. These findings suggest that baseline mucosal cell composition and organization differ between future responders and non-responders, and that filgotinib normalizes mucosal immune cell abundances in full responders. These cellular subsets warrant further investigation for their potential relevance to treatment stratification and pharmacodynamic monitoring of JAK-targeted therapy.

items.title: Agonistic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody improves the antitumor efficacy of a clinical chemo-immunotherapy regimen in a refractory mouse neuroblastoma model.
items.abstract: Background: The current standard regimen for relapsed-refractory high-risk neuroblastoma (HR-NB) is the combination of chemotherapy agents -Temozolomide and Irinotecan - and anti-GD2 antibody dinutuximab (TIG). This treatment results in an overall response for ~40% of patients, but the remaining 60% are resistant to TIG. We hypothesized that agonistic anti-CD40 monoclonal antibody (aCD40), which activates antitumor NK cells and macrophages as we found in previous studies, will improve the efficacy of TIG. Aim: To test the combination of aCD40 and TIG in a mouse HR-NB model that is resistant to TIG. Methods: For these studies, we used a clinically relevant, immunologically cold, HR-NB murine model, 9464D-GD2. Syngeneic mice were intradermally injected with the tumor cells. When tumors were established, mice were randomized and treated with TIG and/or aCD40. Tumor growth and mouse survival were followed. Mice that rejected their tumors were rechallenged to test immunological memory. Changes in immune cells were evaluated by flow cytometry and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNAseq). Results: Similar to ~60% of patients with relapsed/refractory HR-NB, mice bearing 9464D-GD2 tumors did not respond to TIG. Adding aCD40 to TIG induced complete tumor regression in most mice bearing small tumors and extended survival, with many mice remaining tumor-free. The combination of aCD40 and TIG was more effective than aCD40 alone. The antitumor effect of TIG+aCD40 was not inhibited in T cell- or neutrophil-depleted mice but was substantially reduced in NK cell- and macrophage-depleted mice, indicating a role for both NK cells and macrophages in the antitumor effect. Involvement of these cells was consistent with flow cytometry and scRNAseq analyses. Mice treated with TIG+aCD40 that remained tumor-free were rechallenged with 9464D-GD2 cells and showed significantly reduced tumor growth compared to naive mice, indicating a memory response. This memory response was reduced in T cell-depleted mice, indicating the involvement of T cells in memory. Conclusion: These results show that while TIG alone was ineffective, a combination of aCD40 and TIG induced substantial tumor eradication in the 9464D-GD2 tumor model, suggesting that aCD40 may warrant future testing as an addition to the current standard TIG regimen for children with relapsed-refractory HR-NB.

items.title: Integrated multi-omics framework mapping Myeloid associated cellular states (M.A.C.S.)
items.abstract: Functional specialization of myeloid cells in vivo aligns poorly with historic binary classifications. Moreover, inconsistent annotations hinder comparisons across studies. Here, we present Myeloid Associated Cell States (M.A.C.S.), an integrated multiomics framework combining a human Myeloid Cell Atlas (MCA) comprising 498,642 cells from 581 donors across 7 tissues in health and disease with probabilistic mapping of cell populations. Batch-aware variable gene selection preserves tissue-imprinted and disease-associated programs, resolving 24 core states with consensus gene signatures. We introduce scLAVI to quantify population-level similarity with gene-level attribution. These tools resolve resident macrophages into 13 distinct states defined by a combination of a core residence program and tissue-specific programs that are altered upon disease and identify lipid- and scar-associated macrophages as distinct states with complementary roles. M.A.C.S. enables systematic comparison of myeloid cell states across tissues, diseases and experimental activation models, connecting controlled perturbations in vitro to functional specialization in vivo.

items.title: A cross-species single-cell spatial atlas of kidney allografts
items.corresponding_institution: Department of Kidney Transplantation, Zhongshan Hospital, Fudan University; Shanghai Key Laboratory of Organ Transplantation
items.abstract: Kidney allografts with the same Banff diagnosis differ in their immune microenvironments and functional recovery after treatment, yet the tissue features distinguishing recovery from non-recovery remain unclear. We constructed SPECTRA (Spatial Etiology and Coordination of Transplant Rejection in Allografts), which comprises spatial multi-omic data from 1,011,984 cells in 83 human allograft biopsies. We also profiled 442,320 cells from 34 mouse grafts across experimental groups and time points by single-cell sequencing, and integrated a public human single-cell reference of 352,911 cells. Unsupervised analysis identified nine tissue niches, of which plasma-cell effector niche occupancy was associated with less eGFR improvement approximately 90 days after biopsy ({rho} = -0.508, q = 0.0165). Plasma cells in this niche expressed IGHG1, IGKC and TXNDC5; in scarred interstitium, plasma-cell XBP1, HSPA5 and SEC61A1 expression increased with fibrosis. Tertiary lymphoid structures retained TCF7-high stem-like T cells that received CCL19-CCR7 signals from fibroblasts. Using multimodal deep-learning models to delineate anatomical regions, we separated Banff lesions into local immune-load and chronic morphological-injury axes, each with distinct compartmental responses. Peritubular-capillary endothelium increased interferon-{gamma}-associated antigen presentation with local immune load, glomerular endothelium reduced MHC expression with glomerular inflammation, and chronic injury was accompanied by reduced metabolic programmes in specific cell types. In mice, we built a single-cell atlas of kidney transplantation covering syngeneic grafts and BALB/c, DBA/2J and DBA/2N[->]C57BL/6 models. Graft trajectories separated into rejection-associated and tolerance-associated paths that differed in interferon-activated myeloid states and Hnf4a- and Ppara-associated tubular metabolism. In 20 human recipients with rejection-spectrum diagnoses, predictions of functional non-response from a hierarchical causal-inference model were most sensitive to plasma-cell niche occupancy and density. Niche maps predicted from routine H&E were associated with subsequent kidney function. These findings show that kidney allograft rejection is accompanied by changes in cellular states and spatial organisation, and identify plasma-cell niches in residual and scarred interstitium as tissue features of functional non-recovery after rejection.

items.title: Programmed Cell Death-1 marks TOX+ T Regulatory Cells that Inhibit Autoimmunity and Anti-Tumor Immunity
items.abstract: Regulatory T cells (Tregs) are important for the maintenance of immune homeostasis. A proportion of peripheral Tregs constitutively express the coreceptor programmed cell death-1 (PD1), but the importance of this subset is yet to be investigated. We found PD1 marks TOX expressing Tregs. In both PD1 germline deficient and peripheral deficient Tregs, an increase in TOX+ Tregs were noted in steady state which was reproduced in antibody-based blocking studies. We next investigated if TOX+ Tregs were present in disease states. For this we utilised an experimental murine model of melanoma, colorectal cancer and autoimmune colitis. In all experimental conditions, TOX+ Tregs were present and marked by PD-1. To explore the function of PD1+TOX+ Tregs, we utilised a PD1-DTR switch. We found deleting PD1+ Tregs that marked TOX abrogated tumor suppression and enhanced T cell mediated colitis. Mechanistically, we found PD1+TOX+ Treg inhibited the functional plasticity of PD1-Tregs. Taken together, this study identifies PD1 and TOX as markers of Treg function and highlights potential new immunotherapeutic approaches such as PD1+Treg cell depletion for enhanced anti-tumor responses.

items.title: HDAC6 inhibition rewires carbon metabolism to expose an asparagine dependency in multiple myeloma.
items.corresponding_institution: Royal College of Surgeons in Ireland
items.abstract: Multiple myeloma (MM) remains a challenging malignancy with limited therapeutic options upon relapse/refractory disease, necessitating novel combination strategies. Malignant plasma cells sustain continuous immunoglobulin production, a biosynthetic and secretory burden that places heavy demand on central carbon metabolism and creates potentially targetable metabolic vulnerabilities. Previously, we found a role for HDAC6 in modulating glycolytic metabolism. Our goal here was to find induced metabolic vulnerabilities that could be targeted after HDAC6 inhibition or knockdown. Genetic silencing of HDAC6 or pharmacological inhibition with the selective inhibitor BAS-2, suppressed glycolytic flux, reduced pyruvate and lactate labelling from 13C6-glucose, and remodeled mitochondrial morphology in MM cell lines. Global proteomic analysis revealed coordinated upregulation of amino acid transporters (SLC3A2, SLC7A1, SLC1A5, SLC7A5), and spent-medium measurements confirmed an increased depletion of extracellular amino acids. Collectively, this data indicates that BAS-2-treated cells increased their dependence on amino acid import. To identify essential amino acids, we screened MM cells treated with BAS-2 and individually depleted each of the 20 proteinogenic amino acids. Upon depletion of either asparagine, arginine, or aspartate enhanced BAS-2 induced cell death. Combination treatment of BAS-2 and the FDA-approved drug L-asparaginase (L-ASNase), which depletes asparagine, demonstrated synergistic cytotoxicity across a panel of MM cell lines. The combination treatment induces a reliance on asparagine synthesis from pyruvate, as identified by labelling from 13C6-glucose-glucose. Mechanistically the combination induced inhibition of protein synthesis, activated the integrated stress response, and increased ATF4 and CHOP protein expression. Lastly, we showed in vivo in the chick chorioallantoic membrane (CAM) model that BAS-2 and L-ASNase reduced tumour volume and CD138 positivity. In summary, these findings establish HDAC6 inhibition as a translatable metabolic target which rewires amino acid import that can be exploited with L-ASNase in MM.

items.title: EpiCycle: A flexible approach for scalable, three-dimensional reconstructions of complex epithelial tissues
items.abstract: Understanding organ development and repair requires methods to precisely describe cell geometry. Recent image analysis methods allow increasingly accurate segmentation of simple epithelial tissues. However, many vertebrate organs contain more complex stratified epithelia, for which accurate 3D cellular segmentation remains challenging. Here, we describe EpiCycle, an iterative, user-friendly approach developed to address the unique segmentation challenges posed by stratified epithelia. Starting from sparse or no ground truth annotations, EpiCycle guides users through a human-in-the-loop refinement process that culminates in 3D consensus reconstruction. Through cyclical correction, annotation and model retraining, EpiCycle allows users to progressively build robust, dataset-specific segmentation models while simultaneously generating 3D ground truth. To highlight the utility of EpiCycle, we train models that generate high-confidence, tissue-level segmentation of the stratified squamous epithelium in adult zebrafish skin. We apply our approach to segmentation of mouse embryonic branching salivary glands demonstrating its versatility across organs and species. Finally, we produce and analyze quantitative measurements of stratified cell geometry in human fetal epidermis. Thus, EpiCycle enables scalable and quantitative 3D reconstructions of complex vertebrate tissues without relying on pre-existing ground truth.

items.title: Allocating maternal-tree collections to conserve genetic diversity of Lumnitzera littorea in southern Vietnam
items.corresponding_institution: Management Board of Protection and Special-Use Forests of Ho Chi Minh City
items.abstract: Mangrove restoration nurseries often raise seed from a limited number of maternal trees, and how those trees are split among source populations affects which alleles reach the nursery. We genotyped 110 Lumnitzera littorea trees from two mainland and two island sites in southern Vietnam at 11 nuclear microsatellite loci and then enumerated all 5,236 ways of dividing a 30-tree collection among the four sites. With sample sizes matched, the mainland sites had consistently higher expected heterozygosity than the islands. Con Dao and Phu Quoc were the most differentiated pair on the full panel; dropping two influential loci put Can Gio and Phu Quoc at the top instead. Neither pattern changed when we compared the primary genotype calls with an earlier set of calls, restored 23 calls from overlapping adjacent peaks, or removed loci with high estimated null-allele frequencies. Taking 6, 8, 11, and 5 trees from Can Gio, Dong Nai, Con Dao, and Phu Quoc retained an expected 36.89 of 37 alleles on the full panel and 29.94 of 30 on the reduced panel. A nearly even split of 8, 7, 8, and 7 trees gave Phu Quoc better representation and cost little in pooled allele capture. Either split keeps all four provenances in a small collection; which one to use depends on whether a program values the site-private alleles at Con Dao more than balanced representation of every source.

items.title: Uncovering mitochondrial diversity and candidate taxonomic lineages of Hypostomus (Siluriformes: Loricariidae) in Colombia
items.corresponding_institution: Universidad Nacional de Colombia Sede Medellin
items.abstract: Molecular data for Colombian Hypostomus remain sparse, limiting assessments of species boundaries. We combined two mitochondrial markers (cox1 and D-loop) with morphological, morphometric, geographic, and taxonomic evidence to evaluate diversity among Colombian populations. Using ASAP, bPTP, and GMYC, cox1 recovered 16-17 Molecular Operational Taxonomic Units (MOTUs), whereas D-loop yielded 32-37, indicating finer mitochondrial lineage partitioning in D-loop that was not consistently mirrored by phenotypic differentiation. Because both markers belong to the same non-independent mitochondrial linkage group, congruence reflects partition stability rather than independent multi-locus support. High taxonomic-assignment support was obtained for H. holostictus, H. hondae, H. niceforoi, H. plecostomoides, H. oculeus, and H. weberi, whereas H. carinatus, H. hemicochliodon, and H. sculpodon received moderate support and H. wilsoni remained provisional because voucher-linked verification of the sequenced individuals was unavailable. Seven candidate lineages remain unresolved (G1, G2, and M3-M7); M8 was not counted among them because the examined specimens were morphologically compatible with H. hemicochliodon. Among these candidates, Hypostomus sp. G1 and G2 showed method-dependent mitochondrial partitioning and differences in selected morphometric characters relative to examined topotypic H. robinii. G2 also differed in pigmentation from examined H. rhantos, despite morphometric overlap. However, morphometric classification performance in Magdalena specimens and unresolved diagnostic boundaries do not provide sufficient evidence for recognizing G1 and G2 as distinct species. Mitochondrial delimitation patterns can reveal lineage partitioning and help identify taxonomic priorities, but should not be equated with species boundaries. Broader sampling, verified vouchers, and independent nuclear or genomic data are needed to evaluate these taxonomic hypotheses.

items.title: Chromosome-scale comparative genomics reveals a genomic mosaic across the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage
items.abstract: Background: Breeding pedigrees record crosses and selections but do not reveal how the documented relationships are reflected in descendant genomes. Therefore, whole-genome summaries can mask local inheritance patterns generated by recombination and segregation. To examine how documented relationships are reflected across genomic scales, we generated chromosome-scale assemblies of the Hattanso landrace and four cultivars from the documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage of Hiroshima, Japan. We then analyzed genome-wide and local relationships using small variants, structural variants, and gene presence-absence variation. Results: The five assemblies ranged from 375.78 to 378.94 Mb in length, with scaffold N50 values of 30.25-30.43 Mb and 99.8% BUSCO completeness. Single-nucleotide variant data identified Hattan Nos. 10 and 35 as the closest pair at the genome-wide scale, a relationship also supported by protein sequence alignment. This relationship was recovered on 9 of the 12 chromosomes, but genomic relationships varied among local regions. Classification of 500-kb windows based on predefined allele-sharing patterns associated with documented breeding steps assigned 51.91% of the nuclear genome to lineage-pattern categories and identified 143 candidate transition intervals. Publicly available reads from Shuho broadly supported the Hattan No. 35 state, consistent with the recorded Hattan No. 10 x Shuho parentage of Hattan No. 35. Hattan-nishiki Nos. 1 and 2, selected from the recorded Hattan No. 35 x Akitsuho cross, exhibited distinct genomic configurations, with differences across all three variant classes concentrated on Chr12. A 1-Mb region on Chr4 contained single-nucleotide variants, small indels, and structural variants predominantly shared by Hattanso and the four derived cultivars. Functional enrichment analysis of lineage-associated gene sets identified pectinesterase-related functions in the Hattan No. 10-specific set and a diterpenoid-related signal in the Hattan-nishiki No. 2-specific set. Conclusions: The documented Hattan sake-brewing rice lineage exhibits a spatially heterogeneous genomic mosaic, in which a strong genome-wide relationship coexists with local variation in lineage-associated states. Integrating nucleotide-scale, structural, and gene-content variation across genomic scales thus complements pedigree records and helps prioritize candidate regions and genes for future functional and breeding studies.

items.title: Integrated single-cell and bulk transcriptomic analyses of lysine isonicotinylation-related gene expression in diabetic foot ulcer healing
items.corresponding_institution: Secend Affiliated Hospital & Yuying Children's Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University
items.abstract: Diabetic foot ulcers have heterogeneous healing outcomes. We integrated public single-cell and bulk RNA-sequencing datasets to identify cell-type-specific lysine isonicotinylation (Kinic)-related transcriptional patterns and exploratory candidates associated with healing. The atlas comprised 56,568 cells across 14 cell types, with Kinic-related signature scores differing by cell type and healing group. Intersecting bulk differentially expressed genes, single-cell high-versus-low-score differentially expressed genes, and coexpression module genes prioritized LDHB, ISG15, and HAUS1 as exploratory candidates. Seven subtypes were identified among healing-enriched fibroblasts. ISG15-associated enrichment highlighted interferon and inflammatory responses. Simulated deletion of each candidate reduced mean similarity to a non-Healer reference state. Docking identified LDHB ZINC250K 0191530 as the lowest-scoring evaluated pair, while a single 100-ns simulation showed displacement of the ligand from its initial pose. These analyses prioritize LDHB, ISG15, and HAUS1 as exploratory candidates and characterize their cellular context in diabetic foot ulcer healing. Their expression patterns within healing-enriched fibroblasts provide clues to the cellular and molecular differences associated with healing outcomes.

items.title: VS-Suite: Automated Consensus Virtual Screening Platform for Improved Screening of Small Molecules
items.abstract: Growing the recent advances in artificial intelligence and machine leaning (AI&ML) approaches accelerated small molecules screening against targeted proteins with limited computational resources and time. Finding accurate binding pose and affinity prediction is challenges task and traditional docking tools and lacks the reproducibility. Development of the Co-folding model is paradigm shift in drug discovery and development, allowing to predict protein ligand complexes without experimental crystal structures. Notably Boltz-2 predicts the complex structure along with binding affinity directly using protein FASTA sequence and ligand SMILES.
